{"parentUuid":"2546be90-d16a-4893-9e4c-f968f1ca20b9","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c3efc2a3-52e0-4dbd-b89f-42ac058af50a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018o9GDYkeAuhwmChA7L3pYx","type":"tool_result","content":"title:\tSpec: Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS (v1)\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tmaxillamas06-arch\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n\n*Source: the grill session of 2026-10-10 (`/grill-with-docs`, questions Q1–Q17). Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`; decisions respect ADR-001, ADR-002 and ADR-003.*\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nClub de Aficionados Albiazul is an unofficial fan club of Rayados (C.F. Monterrey). Its fans share opinions about the team (how a match went, the lineup, the coach, a signing), but today they post them on X and Facebook, where they are mixed in with everything else and impossible to find again. The fan club wants one place where fan opinions live, organized and easy to read.\n\nThe fan club has one hard rule: no aggression toward people, and no threats against people or places, may ever go public. Tiradera toward rival clubs (Tigres especially) is welcome; a personal attack never is. The leader is the only safeguard, so nothing may reach readers without his check. The leader knows the basics on a computer and nothing technical, so the admin side has to be simple.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Leader** (role *admin*): one person. Checks and publishes everything, writes the fan club's pages, creates and manages accounts, and puts changes online. Not technical.\n- **Member** (role *editor*): a fan with an account, created by the leader. Writes posts and submits them to the leader; cannot publish, cannot touch pages or accounts.\n- **Reader**: any fan visiting the public site on GitHub Pages, usually on a phone. No account; reads only.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves, per ADR-001:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the leader's computer (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, per ADR-002). Members write there; the leader checks, publishes, manages accounts, and runs the site update. Everything people see is in Spanish.\n- A **public site**: static HTML regenerated from published content only and deployed to GitHub Pages. A home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, a page per post, and the fan club's pages in the menu. Navy-and-white, playful, unmistakably Monterrey, never official.\n\nEvery change readers can see passes through the leader (ADR-003): posts move draft → submitted → published, a member's change to a published post waits as a pending edit, and a member's nickname is chosen once.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login.** The leader and members sign in with email and password and sign out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong email and a wrong password get the same message.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* = the leader: everything. *Editor* = a member: writes, edits and submits their own posts, reads everyone's posts, proposes edits to their own published posts. Editors cannot publish, cannot see or change pages, cannot manage accounts, and cannot run a site update. Enforced on the server for every route, never by hiding links.\n3. **Posts.** A post is a fan's opinion: title, slug, Markdown body, exactly one topic, status (draft, submitted, published), author, and created/updated/published timestamps. Full create, read, update, delete, following the lifecycle below.\n4. **Pages.** Fixed fan-club information: same fields as a post minus the topic, plus a menu-order number. Only the leader creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes and deletes them. Published pages appear in the public menu in menu order.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a content list filterable by status, topic and (leader only) post vs page, and an editor with a *Vista previa* that shows the sanitized result.\n6. **User management.** Leader only: create accounts, change roles, set a nickname, set a new temporary password, deactivate and reactivate. A deactivated user cannot log in, and an existing session stops working on its next request.\n7. **Public site and site update.** `cms publish` regenerates the public site from published posts and pages only, with sanitized Markdown, a menu built from published pages, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The leader's *Actualizar el sitio* button does both.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Leader\n\n1. As the leader, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use the leader's powers.\n2. As the leader, I want a dashboard showing how many posts are waiting for review, so that I know at a glance whether I have checking to do.\n3. As the leader, I want the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts, pending edits, pages and active members, so that I can see the state of the site without opening lists.\n4. As the leader, I want the dashboard to show when the site was last updated, so that I know whether readers are seeing my latest decisions.\n5. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to submitted posts, so that my review queue is one click away.\n6. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to posts with a pending edit, so that I can review changes to published posts.\n7. As the leader, I want to filter the content list by topic and by post vs page, so that I can find things quickly.\n8. As the leader, I want to read a submitted post exactly as readers would see it, so that I can judge whether it crosses from tiradera into a personal attack.\n9. As the leader, I want to publish a submitted post, so that it goes public at the next site update.\n10. As the leader, I want to send back a submitted post to draft, so that its member can rework it.\n11. As the leader, I want to see a pending edit side by side with the published version, so that I can judge exactly what would change.\n12. As the leader, I want to approve a pending edit, so that the improved version replaces the published one.\n13. As the leader, I want to send back a pending edit, so that the published version stays untouched.\n14. As the leader, I want to unpublish a published post, so that it disappears from the public site at the next site update.\n15. As the leader, I want to be stopped from unpublishing a post while a pending edit waits, so that a member's proposed change is never silently thrown away.\n16. As the leader, I want to edit any post directly, so that I can fix a typo without a round trip; my edits to published posts go live at the next site update.\n17. As the leader, I want to write my own posts and publish them directly, so that fan club news does not wait on a review of myself.\n18. As the leader, I want to delete any post after confirming, so that content that should never have existed is gone.\n19. As the leader, I want to create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete pages, so that *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa* and *Cómo unirse* stay accurate.\n20. As the leader, I want to set each page's menu-order number, so that the public menu reads in the order I choose.\n21. As the leader, I want to be prevented from giving a page a name the site already uses (such as the home page or a topic page), so that nothing on the site is overwritten.\n22. As the leader, I want to create a member account with an email, role and temporary password, so that a fan who asked to join can start writing.\n23. As the leader, I want to promote a member to admin or demote an admin to editor, so that I can share the job if I need to.\n24. As the leader, I want to be unable to remove my own admin role or deactivate myself, so that I cannot lock myself out.\n25. As the leader, I want to deactivate an account, so that a member who breaks the house rules can no longer log in.\n26. As the leader, I want to reactivate an account, so that a member can come back.\n27. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's posts to stay up under their nickname, so that the fan club's archive is not broken.\n28. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's submitted posts and pending edits to stay in my queue, so that I still decide what happens to them.\n29. As the leader, I want to change any member's nickname, so that I can fix a nickname that breaks the house rules.\n30. As the leader, I want to set a new temporary password for a member, so that a member who forgot theirs can get back in.\n31. As the leader, I want one *Actualizar el sitio* button that regenerates the public site and uploads it, so that I never need a terminal.\n32. As the leader, I want the button to tell me in plain Spanish what happened at each step, so that I know whether readers can see my changes or what went wrong.\n33. As the leader, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I always know whether my action worked.\n\n### Member\n\n34. As a member, I want to log in with the email and temporary password the leader gave me, so that I can start writing.\n35. As a member, I want to choose my nickname at my first login, so that readers know me by the name I picked.\n36. As a member, I want the site to refuse a nickname someone else already uses, so that nobody can pass as me or I as them.\n37. As a member, I want to change my password on *Mi cuenta*, so that the leader no longer knows it.\n38. As a member, I want to write a post with a title, a topic and a Markdown body, so that I can share my opinion.\n39. As a member, I want the slug to be made from my title, keeping accents and ñ, so that the link reads like my title.\n40. As a member, I want to edit the slug until my post is first published, so that I can tidy the link.\n41. As a member, I want to press *Vista previa* and see exactly what readers will see, so that my formatting is right before I submit.\n42. As a member, I want to save a draft and come back later, so that I can finish a match opinion the next morning.\n43. As a member, I want to submit a finished draft to the leader, so that he knows it is ready to check.\n44. As a member, I want to withdraw a submitted post back to draft, so that I can fix something before the leader reads it.\n45. As a member, I want to delete my own draft, so that I can drop an opinion I changed my mind about.\n46. As a member, I want to propose an edit to my own published post, so that I can correct it while the published version stays up.\n47. As a member, I want my new pending edit to replace my previous one, so that the leader always sees my latest proposal.\n48. As a member, I want to see every post in the content list, including other members', so that I know what has already been written about Saturday's match.\n49. As a member, I want to be refused when I try to change someone else's post or reach a leader screen, so that the rules are real.\n50. As a member, I want a clear \"no tienes permiso\" page when I am refused, so that I understand what happened.\n\n### Reader\n\n51. As a reader, I want a home page with one section per topic showing its three newest posts, so that I can see what fans are saying about each subject.\n52. As a reader, I want a *Ver todos* link on each section, so that I can read every post in a topic.\n53. As a reader, I want each post to show its title, the author's nickname, its topic, and *Publicado el …* (and *Actualizado el …* if it changed after publishing), so that I know who said what and when.\n54. As a reader, I want the menu to list the fan club's pages, so that I can find the house rules and how to join.\n55. As a reader, I want to read *Reglas de la casa*, so that I know where the line between tiradera and a personal attack is.\n56. As a reader, I want *Cómo unirse* to tell me how to ask the leader for an account, so that I can start writing too.\n57. As a reader, I want the site to work on my phone without sideways scrolling, so that I can read it at the stadium.\n58. As a reader, I want links to keep working after I share them on X or Facebook, so that my friends land on the same post.\n59. As a reader, I want to see the disclaimer on every page, so that nobody mistakes the site for an official Rayados site.\n60. As a reader, I never want to see drafts, submitted posts, pending edits, or anything the leader has not approved.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Modules\n\nDeep modules with small interfaces; the web layer stays thin.\n\n- **Accounts.** Password hashing and verification (argon2), login, logout, session handling, loading the current user on every request and rejecting deactivated users, nickname rules, and the user-management operations. Interface: authenticate(email, password) → user or failure; current_user(request); create/update/deactivate/reactivate operations that enforce the self-lockout rules.\n- **Policy.** The single place that answers \"may this person do this action to this item?\" from role, ownership and status. Every write route asks it; templates may use it to hide buttons, but hiding is never the control.\n- **Content.** Posts, pages and pending edits: storage, slug generation, and the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions (table below). Invalid transitions are refused here, not in the routes.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function: Markdown text in, sanitized HTML out (markdown-it-py, then nh3 with an allowlist). Used by *Vista previa*, the leader's review screens and the site export, so the preview is always exactly what readers get.\n- **Site export.** Renders every published post and published page, the topic pages and the home page into an output directory with relative, percent-encoded links. Called by `cms publish` and by the site update.\n- **Site update.** Export, then deploy (push the output to the `gh-pages` branch), then record the time of the last site update. The deploy step is injectable so tests never push. Called by *Actualizar el sitio* and mirrored by the `cms publish` / `cms deploy` CLI.\n- **Admin web layer.** Routes and Spanish templates for login, first-login nickname, *Mi cuenta*, dashboard, content list, post editor, page editor, review screens, users, site update, and the refusal page.\n- **Public templates.** Home, topic page, post page, page, shared layout with menu, topic links and disclaimer.\n- **Seed.** Rebuilds the demo database from scratch with fictional data.\n\n### Data model\n\n- **User**: id, email (unique, used to log in), password hash (argon2), nickname (unique ignoring case; empty until chosen), role (*admin* or *editor*), active flag, created and updated timestamps.\n- **Post**: id, title, slug (unique among posts), Markdown body, topic, status (*draft*, *submitted*, *published*), author (a user), created and updated timestamps, first-published timestamp (set once, never cleared; its presence locks the slug), and an edited-after-publishing timestamp (drives *Actualizado el …*).\n- **Pending edit**: at most one per post; proposed title, topic and Markdown body, created and updated timestamps. The slug is never part of a pending edit.\n- **Page**: id, title, slug (unique among pages, and never a reserved name), Markdown body, status (*draft* or *published*), menu-order number, author, created, updated and first-published timestamps.\n- **Site state**: the time of the last successful export.\n- **Topics** are a fixed list in code, not a table: Match (*Partido*), Lineup (*Alineación*), Coach (*Técnico*), Signings (*Fichajes*), Fan club news (*Noticias del club de aficionados*).\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n| Action | Who | From | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Save | the member who wrote it; the leader | draft | stays draft |\n| Submit | the member who wrote it | draft | submitted |\n| Withdraw | the member who wrote it | submitted | draft |\n| Publish | leader | draft or submitted | published; sets first-published the first time |\n| Send back | leader | submitted | draft |\n| Unpublish | leader | published, with no pending edit | draft |\n| Propose edit | the member who wrote it | published | stays published; creates or replaces its pending edit |\n| Approve | leader | pending edit | the edit replaces title, topic and body; pending edit removed; edited-after-publishing set |\n| Send back (pending edit) | leader | pending edit | pending edit removed; published version untouched |\n| Edit directly | leader | any status | same status; if published, sets edited-after-publishing |\n| Delete | the member who wrote it, drafts only; the leader, any post | any | post and its pending edit removed |\n\nThe leader's own posts may be published straight from draft. A member never changes a submitted or published post directly. A member may read every post in the admin console but act only on their own.\n\nPages have two statuses only (*draft*, *published*) and no submitted step, because only the leader writes them.\n\n### Accounts and access\n\n- Login identifier is the email. The test helper in `tests/conftest.py` already posts `email` and `password` to `/login`; its demo users are updated to match the seed's emails.\n- Wrong email and wrong password both show *\"Correo o contraseña incorrectos.\"*\n- Sessions use a signed, HTTP-only, same-site cookie holding the user id and a CSRF token. The user is reloaded on every request, so deactivation takes effect immediately.\n- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token in a hidden field, including login, logout, *Vista previa* and the site update. A POST without a valid token gets 403.\n- Anonymous requests to any admin route redirect to `/login`. An editor requesting a leader-only route, or acting on someone else's post, gets 403 with a Spanish refusal page that keeps the admin menu. Unknown ids get 404.\n- A user without a nickname is sent to the first-login nickname screen before anything else. Seeded users already have nicknames so the judge's walkthrough is never interrupted.\n- Nickname: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case; afterwards only the leader can change it.\n- Passwords: at least 8 characters when set or changed.\n- The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate themselves. Users are never deleted.\n\n### Admin routes (contract)\n\nPaths and form field names are English; everything people read is Spanish.\n\n- `/login` (GET, POST), `/logout` (POST)\n- `/admin` dashboard; `/admin/nickname` first-login nickname; `/admin/account` *Mi cuenta*\n- `/admin/content` content list with `status`, `topic`, `pending` and (leader only) `type` filters\n- `/admin/posts/new`, `/admin/posts/{id}` and one POST route per lifecycle action, plus a preview POST\n- `/admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit` side-by-side review (leader)\n- `/admin/pages/...` create, edit, publish, unpublish, delete, preview (leader only)\n- `/admin/users/...` list, create, change role, set nickname, set temporary password, deactivate, reactivate (leader only)\n- `/admin/site-update` (POST, leader only)\n\nEvery leader-only route is declared as such in one place, so a test can enumerate all of them.\n\n### Slugs\n\nMade from the title: Unicode-normalized (NFC), lowercased, letters (including á é í ó ú ü ñ) and digits kept, every other run of characters replaced by a single hyphen, trimmed, capped at 80 characters. Example: *\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\"* → `crónica-del-clásico-regio`. A taken slug gets `-2`, `-3`, … A manually entered slug follows the same rules. A post's slug is editable until it is first published, then locked forever, so shared links keep working. Page slugs may not be a reserved name: `index`, `tema`, `posts`, `style`.\n\n### Markdown\n\nRendered with markdown-it-py, then sanitized with nh3 using an allowlist of text-formatting tags, lists, blockquotes, code and links. Scripts, event-handler attributes and `javascript:` links are removed. **Images are removed too**: photo uploads are out of scope and the site must carry no official photos. Links get `rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"`.\n---\n# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Account** (*Cuenta*):\nA leader's or member's way into the admin console: an email, a password, a role, a nickname, and whether it is active. Never deleted. *Mi cuenta* is where a person sees their own.\n_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login\n\n**Temporary password** (*Contraseña temporal*):\nA password the leader sets on an account and hands over in person, for a new member or one who forgot theirs. The member can replace it on *Mi cuenta*.\n_Avoid_: Default password, reset link\n\n**Deactivate** (*Desactivar*):\nThe leader closing an account without deleting it: its person can no longer sign in, and their posts stay under their nickname. **Reactivate** (*Reactivar*) opens it again.\n_Avoid_: Delete, ban, block, suspend\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post** (*Publicación*):\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic. In Spanish, *publicación* is always the thing, never the act: for the act say *publicar*.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry; \"la publicación de …\" to mean publishing\n\n**Slug** (*Enlace*):\nThe end of a post's or page's web address, made from its title (`crónica-del-clásico-regio`). It can be changed until the post or page is first published, then never, so links shared on X or Facebook keep working. A page's slug can never be a name the site already uses for itself (the home page, the topic pages).\n_Avoid_: URL, permalink, path\n\n**Preview** (*Vista previa*):\nA post's Markdown shown exactly as readers will see it, sanitized, without saving anything.\n_Avoid_: Draft view, render\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page** (*Página*):\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted. A page is a draft until the leader publishes it; unpublishing takes it back out of the menu at the next site update. Members never see pages in the admin console.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*):\nThe number the leader gives each page. The public menu lists *Inicio*, then the published pages from the lowest number up.\n_Avoid_: Position, weight, rank\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft** (*Borrador*):\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted** (*Enviada*):\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public. The dashboard counts these as *Esperando revisión* (waiting for review). With pending edits, they make up the leader's review queue.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published** (*Publicada*):\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back** (*Devolver*):\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish** (*Despublicar*):\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next site update. The slug stays locked.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit** (*Cambios propuestos*):\nA member's proposed change to a published post (title, topic, body; never the slug), waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit. The dashboard counts these as *Cambios propuestos*.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve** (*Aprobar*):\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version. Readers then see *Actualizado el …* on the post, as they do after the leader edits a published post directly.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n**Site update** (*Actualizar el sitio*):\nThe leader regenerating the public site from everything published and putting it online. Readers see nothing new until a site update; publishing alone changes nothing they can see.\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), deploy, build, export\n\n**Export**:\nThe first half of a site update: writing the public site's files from everything published, wiping what was there (`cms publish`). The dashboard shows when the last one happened (*Sitio generado por última vez*).\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), build, render\n\n**Upload** (*Subir*):\nThe second half of a site update: putting the exported files online on GitHub Pages (`cms deploy`). If it fails, the export still stands and readers keep the previous site.\n_Avoid_: Deploy (in prose), push, publish\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"3fedac67-b247-411d-847f-43bb6bfefb65","timestamp":"2026-10-15T19:59:44.101Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"title:\tSpec: Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS (v1)\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tmaxillamas06-arch\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n\n*Source: the grill session of 2026-10-10 (`/grill-with-docs`, questions Q1–Q17). Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`; decisions respect ADR-001, ADR-002 and ADR-003.*\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nClub de Aficionados Albiazul is an unofficial fan club of Rayados (C.F. Monterrey). Its fans share opinions about the team (how a match went, the lineup, the coach, a signing), but today they post them on X and Facebook, where they are mixed in with everything else and impossible to find again. The fan club wants one place where fan opinions live, organized and easy to read.\n\nThe fan club has one hard rule: no aggression toward people, and no threats against people or places, may ever go public. Tiradera toward rival clubs (Tigres especially) is welcome; a personal attack never is. The leader is the only safeguard, so nothing may reach readers without his check. The leader knows the basics on a computer and nothing technical, so the admin side has to be simple.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Leader** (role *admin*): one person. Checks and publishes everything, writes the fan club's pages, creates and manages accounts, and puts changes online. Not technical.\n- **Member** (role *editor*): a fan with an account, created by the leader. Writes posts and submits them to the leader; cannot publish, cannot touch pages or accounts.\n- **Reader**: any fan visiting the public site on GitHub Pages, usually on a phone. No account; reads only.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves, per ADR-001:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the leader's computer (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, per ADR-002). Members write there; the leader checks, publishes, manages accounts, and runs the site update. Everything people see is in Spanish.\n- A **public site**: static HTML regenerated from published content only and deployed to GitHub Pages. A home page with one section per topic, a page per topic, a page per post, and the fan club's pages in the menu. Navy-and-white, playful, unmistakably Monterrey, never official.\n\nEvery change readers can see passes through the leader (ADR-003): posts move draft → submitted → published, a member's change to a published post waits as a pending edit, and a member's nickname is chosen once.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login.** The leader and members sign in with email and password and sign out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong email and a wrong password get the same message.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* = the leader: everything. *Editor* = a member: writes, edits and submits their own posts, reads everyone's posts, proposes edits to their own published posts. Editors cannot publish, cannot see or change pages, cannot manage accounts, and cannot run a site update. Enforced on the server for every route, never by hiding links.\n3. **Posts.** A post is a fan's opinion: title, slug, Markdown body, exactly one topic, status (draft, submitted, published), author, and created/updated/published timestamps. Full create, read, update, delete, following the lifecycle below.\n4. **Pages.** Fixed fan-club information: same fields as a post minus the topic, plus a menu-order number. Only the leader creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes and deletes them. Published pages appear in the public menu in menu order.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a content list filterable by status, topic and (leader only) post vs page, and an editor with a *Vista previa* that shows the sanitized result.\n6. **User management.** Leader only: create accounts, change roles, set a nickname, set a new temporary password, deactivate and reactivate. A deactivated user cannot log in, and an existing session stops working on its next request.\n7. **Public site and site update.** `cms publish` regenerates the public site from published posts and pages only, with sanitized Markdown, a menu built from published pages, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The leader's *Actualizar el sitio* button does both.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Leader\n\n1. As the leader, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use the leader's powers.\n2. As the leader, I want a dashboard showing how many posts are waiting for review, so that I know at a glance whether I have checking to do.\n3. As the leader, I want the dashboard to count drafts, submitted posts, published posts, pending edits, pages and active members, so that I can see the state of the site without opening lists.\n4. As the leader, I want the dashboard to show when the site was last updated, so that I know whether readers are seeing my latest decisions.\n5. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to submitted posts, so that my review queue is one click away.\n6. As the leader, I want to filter the content list to posts with a pending edit, so that I can review changes to published posts.\n7. As the leader, I want to filter the content list by topic and by post vs page, so that I can find things quickly.\n8. As the leader, I want to read a submitted post exactly as readers would see it, so that I can judge whether it crosses from tiradera into a personal attack.\n9. As the leader, I want to publish a submitted post, so that it goes public at the next site update.\n10. As the leader, I want to send back a submitted post to draft, so that its member can rework it.\n11. As the leader, I want to see a pending edit side by side with the published version, so that I can judge exactly what would change.\n12. As the leader, I want to approve a pending edit, so that the improved version replaces the published one.\n13. As the leader, I want to send back a pending edit, so that the published version stays untouched.\n14. As the leader, I want to unpublish a published post, so that it disappears from the public site at the next site update.\n15. As the leader, I want to be stopped from unpublishing a post while a pending edit waits, so that a member's proposed change is never silently thrown away.\n16. As the leader, I want to edit any post directly, so that I can fix a typo without a round trip; my edits to published posts go live at the next site update.\n17. As the leader, I want to write my own posts and publish them directly, so that fan club news does not wait on a review of myself.\n18. As the leader, I want to delete any post after confirming, so that content that should never have existed is gone.\n19. As the leader, I want to create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete pages, so that *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa* and *Cómo unirse* stay accurate.\n20. As the leader, I want to set each page's menu-order number, so that the public menu reads in the order I choose.\n21. As the leader, I want to be prevented from giving a page a name the site already uses (such as the home page or a topic page), so that nothing on the site is overwritten.\n22. As the leader, I want to create a member account with an email, role and temporary password, so that a fan who asked to join can start writing.\n23. As the leader, I want to promote a member to admin or demote an admin to editor, so that I can share the job if I need to.\n24. As the leader, I want to be unable to remove my own admin role or deactivate myself, so that I cannot lock myself out.\n25. As the leader, I want to deactivate an account, so that a member who breaks the house rules can no longer log in.\n26. As the leader, I want to reactivate an account, so that a member can come back.\n27. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's posts to stay up under their nickname, so that the fan club's archive is not broken.\n28. As the leader, I want a deactivated member's submitted posts and pending edits to stay in my queue, so that I still decide what happens to them.\n29. As the leader, I want to change any member's nickname, so that I can fix a nickname that breaks the house rules.\n30. As the leader, I want to set a new temporary password for a member, so that a member who forgot theirs can get back in.\n31. As the leader, I want one *Actualizar el sitio* button that regenerates the public site and uploads it, so that I never need a terminal.\n32. As the leader, I want the button to tell me in plain Spanish what happened at each step, so that I know whether readers can see my changes or what went wrong.\n33. As the leader, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I always know whether my action worked.\n\n### Member\n\n34. As a member, I want to log in with the email and temporary password the leader gave me, so that I can start writing.\n35. As a member, I want to choose my nickname at my first login, so that readers know me by the name I picked.\n36. As a member, I want the site to refuse a nickname someone else already uses, so that nobody can pass as me or I as them.\n37. As a member, I want to change my password on *Mi cuenta*, so that the leader no longer knows it.\n38. As a member, I want to write a post with a title, a topic and a Markdown body, so that I can share my opinion.\n39. As a member, I want the slug to be made from my title, keeping accents and ñ, so that the link reads like my title.\n40. As a member, I want to edit the slug until my post is first published, so that I can tidy the link.\n41. As a member, I want to press *Vista previa* and see exactly what readers will see, so that my formatting is right before I submit.\n42. As a member, I want to save a draft and come back later, so that I can finish a match opinion the next morning.\n43. As a member, I want to submit a finished draft to the leader, so that he knows it is ready to check.\n44. As a member, I want to withdraw a submitted post back to draft, so that I can fix something before the leader reads it.\n45. As a member, I want to delete my own draft, so that I can drop an opinion I changed my mind about.\n46. As a member, I want to propose an edit to my own published post, so that I can correct it while the published version stays up.\n47. As a member, I want my new pending edit to replace my previous one, so that the leader always sees my latest proposal.\n48. As a member, I want to see every post in the content list, including other members', so that I know what has already been written about Saturday's match.\n49. As a member, I want to be refused when I try to change someone else's post or reach a leader screen, so that the rules are real.\n50. As a member, I want a clear \"no tienes permiso\" page when I am refused, so that I understand what happened.\n\n### Reader\n\n51. As a reader, I want a home page with one section per topic showing its three newest posts, so that I can see what fans are saying about each subject.\n52. As a reader, I want a *Ver todos* link on each section, so that I can read every post in a topic.\n53. As a reader, I want each post to show its title, the author's nickname, its topic, and *Publicado el …* (and *Actualizado el …* if it changed after publishing), so that I know who said what and when.\n54. As a reader, I want the menu to list the fan club's pages, so that I can find the house rules and how to join.\n55. As a reader, I want to read *Reglas de la casa*, so that I know where the line between tiradera and a personal attack is.\n56. As a reader, I want *Cómo unirse* to tell me how to ask the leader for an account, so that I can start writing too.\n57. As a reader, I want the site to work on my phone without sideways scrolling, so that I can read it at the stadium.\n58. As a reader, I want links to keep working after I share them on X or Facebook, so that my friends land on the same post.\n59. As a reader, I want to see the disclaimer on every page, so that nobody mistakes the site for an official Rayados site.\n60. As a reader, I never want to see drafts, submitted posts, pending edits, or anything the leader has not approved.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Modules\n\nDeep modules with small interfaces; the web layer stays thin.\n\n- **Accounts.** Password hashing and verification (argon2), login, logout, session handling, loading the current user on every request and rejecting deactivated users, nickname rules, and the user-management operations. Interface: authenticate(email, password) → user or failure; current_user(request); create/update/deactivate/reactivate operations that enforce the self-lockout rules.\n- **Policy.** The single place that answers \"may this person do this action to this item?\" from role, ownership and status. Every write route asks it; templates may use it to hide buttons, but hiding is never the control.\n- **Content.** Posts, pages and pending edits: storage, slug generation, and the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions (table below). Invalid transitions are refused here, not in the routes.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function: Markdown text in, sanitized HTML out (markdown-it-py, then nh3 with an allowlist). Used by *Vista previa*, the leader's review screens and the site export, so the preview is always exactly what readers get.\n- **Site export.** Renders every published post and published page, the topic pages and the home page into an output directory with relative, percent-encoded links. Called by `cms publish` and by the site update.\n- **Site update.** Export, then deploy (push the output to the `gh-pages` branch), then record the time of the last site update. The deploy step is injectable so tests never push. Called by *Actualizar el sitio* and mirrored by the `cms publish` / `cms deploy` CLI.\n- **Admin web layer.** Routes and Spanish templates for login, first-login nickname, *Mi cuenta*, dashboard, content list, post editor, page editor, review screens, users, site update, and the refusal page.\n- **Public templates.** Home, topic page, post page, page, shared layout with menu, topic links and disclaimer.\n- **Seed.** Rebuilds the demo database from scratch with fictional data.\n\n### Data model\n\n- **User**: id, email (unique, used to log in), password hash (argon2), nickname (unique ignoring case; empty until chosen), role (*admin* or *editor*), active flag, created and updated timestamps.\n- **Post**: id, title, slug (unique among posts), Markdown body, topic, status (*draft*, *submitted*, *published*), author (a user), created and updated timestamps, first-published timestamp (set once, never cleared; its presence locks the slug), and an edited-after-publishing timestamp (drives *Actualizado el …*).\n- **Pending edit**: at most one per post; proposed title, topic and Markdown body, created and updated timestamps. The slug is never part of a pending edit.\n- **Page**: id, title, slug (unique among pages, and never a reserved name), Markdown body, status (*draft* or *published*), menu-order number, author, created, updated and first-published timestamps.\n- **Site state**: the time of the last successful export.\n- **Topics** are a fixed list in code, not a table: Match (*Partido*), Lineup (*Alineación*), Coach (*Técnico*), Signings (*Fichajes*), Fan club news (*Noticias del club de aficionados*).\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n| Action | Who | From | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Save | the member who wrote it; the leader | draft | stays draft |\n| Submit | the member who wrote it | draft | submitted |\n| Withdraw | the member who wrote it | submitted | draft |\n| Publish | leader | draft or submitted | published; sets first-published the first time |\n| Send back | leader | submitted | draft |\n| Unpublish | leader | published, with no pending edit | draft |\n| Propose edit | the member who wrote it | published | stays published; creates or replaces its pending edit |\n| Approve | leader | pending edit | the edit replaces title, topic and body; pending edit removed; edited-after-publishing set |\n| Send back (pending edit) | leader | pending edit | pending edit removed; published version untouched |\n| Edit directly | leader | any status | same status; if published, sets edited-after-publishing |\n| Delete | the member who wrote it, drafts only; the leader, any post | any | post and its pending edit removed |\n\nThe leader's own posts may be published straight from draft. A member never changes a submitted or published post directly. A member may read every post in the admin console but act only on their own.\n\nPages have two statuses only (*draft*, *published*) and no submitted step, because only the leader writes them.\n\n### Accounts and access\n\n- Login identifier is the email. The test helper in `tests/conftest.py` already posts `email` and `password` to `/login`; its demo users are updated to match the seed's emails.\n- Wrong email and wrong password both show *\"Correo o contraseña incorrectos.\"*\n- Sessions use a signed, HTTP-only, same-site cookie holding the user id and a CSRF token. The user is reloaded on every request, so deactivation takes effect immediately.\n- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token in a hidden field, including login, logout, *Vista previa* and the site update. A POST without a valid token gets 403.\n- Anonymous requests to any admin route redirect to `/login`. An editor requesting a leader-only route, or acting on someone else's post, gets 403 with a Spanish refusal page that keeps the admin menu. Unknown ids get 404.\n- A user without a nickname is sent to the first-login nickname screen before anything else. Seeded users already have nicknames so the judge's walkthrough is never interrupted.\n- Nickname: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case; afterwards only the leader can change it.\n- Passwords: at least 8 characters when set or changed.\n- The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate themselves. Users are never deleted.\n\n### Admin routes (contract)\n\nPaths and form field names are English; everything people read is Spanish.\n\n- `/login` (GET, POST), `/logout` (POST)\n- `/admin` dashboard; `/admin/nickname` first-login nickname; `/admin/account` *Mi cuenta*\n- `/admin/content` content list with `status`, `topic`, `pending` and (leader only) `type` filters\n- `/admin/posts/new`, `/admin/posts/{id}` and one POST route per lifecycle action, plus a preview POST\n- `/admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit` side-by-side review (leader)\n- `/admin/pages/...` create, edit, publish, unpublish, delete, preview (leader only)\n- `/admin/users/...` list, create, change role, set nickname, set temporary password, deactivate, reactivate (leader only)\n- `/admin/site-update` (POST, leader only)\n\nEvery leader-only route is declared as such in one place, so a test can enumerate all of them.\n\n### Slugs\n\nMade from the title: Unicode-normalized (NFC), lowercased, letters (including á é í ó ú ü ñ) and digits kept, every other run of characters replaced by a single hyphen, trimmed, capped at 80 characters. Example: *\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\"* → `crónica-del-clásico-regio`. A taken slug gets `-2`, `-3`, … A manually entered slug follows the same rules. A post's slug is editable until it is first published, then locked forever, so shared links keep working. Page slugs may not be a reserved name: `index`, `tema`, `posts`, `style`.\n\n### Markdown\n\nRendered with markdown-it-py, then sanitized with nh3 using an allowlist of text-formatting tags, lists, blockquotes, code and links. Scripts, event-handler attributes and `javascript:` links are removed. **Images are removed too**: photo uploads are out of scope and the site must carry no official photos. Links get `rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"`.\n---\n# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Account** (*Cuenta*):\nA leader's or member's way into the admin console: an email, a password, a role, a nickname, and whether it is active. Never deleted. *Mi cuenta* is where a person sees their own.\n_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login\n\n**Temporary password** (*Contraseña temporal*):\nA password the leader sets on an account and hands over in person, for a new member or one who forgot theirs. The member can replace it on *Mi cuenta*.\n_Avoid_: Default password, reset link\n\n**Deactivate** (*Desactivar*):\nThe leader closing an account without deleting it: its person can no longer sign in, and their posts stay under their nickname. **Reactivate** (*Reactivar*) opens it again.\n_Avoid_: Delete, ban, block, suspend\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post** (*Publicación*):\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic. In Spanish, *publicación* is always the thing, never the act: for the act say *publicar*.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry; \"la publicación de …\" to mean publishing\n\n**Slug** (*Enlace*):\nThe end of a post's or page's web address, made from its title (`crónica-del-clásico-regio`). It can be changed until the post or page is first published, then never, so links shared on X or Facebook keep working. A page's slug can never be a name the site already uses for itself (the home page, the topic pages).\n_Avoid_: URL, permalink, path\n\n**Preview** (*Vista previa*):\nA post's Markdown shown exactly as readers will see it, sanitized, without saving anything.\n_Avoid_: Draft view, render\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page** (*Página*):\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted. A page is a draft until the leader publishes it; unpublishing takes it back out of the menu at the next site update. Members never see pages in the admin console.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*):\nThe number the leader gives each page. The public menu lists *Inicio*, then the published pages from the lowest number up.\n_Avoid_: Position, weight, rank\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft** (*Borrador*):\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted** (*Enviada*):\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public. The dashboard counts these as *Esperando revisión* (waiting for review). With pending edits, they make up the leader's review queue.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published** (*Publicada*):\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back** (*Devolver*):\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish** (*Despublicar*):\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next site update. The slug stays locked.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit** (*Cambios propuestos*):\nA member's proposed change to a published post (title, topic, body; never the slug), waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit. The dashboard counts these as *Cambios propuestos*.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve** (*Aprobar*):\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version. Readers then see *Actualizado el …* on the post, as they do after the leader edits a published post directly.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n**Site update** (*Actualizar el sitio*):\nThe leader regenerating the public site from everything published and putting it online. Readers see nothing new until a site update; publishing alone changes nothing they can see.\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), deploy, build, export\n\n**Export**:\nThe first half of a site update: writing the public site's files from everything published, wiping what was there (`cms publish`). The dashboard shows when the last one happened (*Sitio generado por última vez*).\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), build, render\n\n**Upload** (*Subir*):\nThe second half of a site update: putting the exported files online on GitHub Pages (`cms deploy`). If it fails, the export still stands and readers keep the previous site.\n_Avoid_: Deploy (in prose), push, publish\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2546be90-d16a-4893-9e4c-f968f1ca20b9","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"b1238ded-4505-409e-821a-99d1cfa3d487","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c3efc2a3-52e0-4dbd-b89f-42ac058af50a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KNjdwAfaj2dULa6Co2EJ9v","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Site export: the public site, written as static HTML from published content only.\n\n`cms publish` and the leader's site update call export_site(), which also records\nwhen it ran, for the dashboard. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED posts and pages are written. A draft that reaches the output\n     is a bug.\n  2. Every href is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"../posts/x.html\"), never root-absolute\n     (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves the site from a subfolder. Links are\n     percent-encoded too, so slugs with accents and ñ never break.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\nfrom urllib.parse import quote\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content, db, markdown, settings\nfrom app.content import Page, Post\nfrom app.dates import spanish_date\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass TopicPage:\n    \"\"\"A topic's public page: every published post filed under it, newest first.\"\"\"\n    name: str\n    path: str  # where it is written, from the site root: \"tema/alineación.html\"\n    posts: list[Post]\n\n\ndef post_path(post: Post) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Where a post's page is written, from the site root.\"\"\"\n    return f\"posts/{post.slug}.html\"\n\n\ndef page_path(page: Page) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Where a page is written: at the site root, beside the home page.\"\"\"\n    return f\"{page.slug}.html\"\n\n\ndef export_site(conn: sqlite3.Connection, out: Path) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Wipe `out`, write the public site into it, and record when; returns how many\n    posts it holds.\"\"\"\n    posts = content.published_posts(conn)\n    pages = content.published_pages(conn)\n    topics = {key: TopicPage(name, f\"tema/{content.slugify(name)}.html\",\n                             [post for post in posts if post.topic == key])\n              for key, name in content.TOPICS.items()}\n\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    shutil.copyfile(settings.TEMPLATES / \"public\" / \"style.css\", out / \"style.css\")\n    env = _environment(list(topics.values()), pages)\n    _write(env, out, \"index.html\", \"public/home.html\")\n    for topic in topics.values():  # all five, even when empty, so no topic link breaks\n        _write(env, out, topic.path, \"public/topic.html\", topic=topic)\n    for post in posts:\n        _write(env, out, post_path(post), \"public/post.html\", post=post,\n               topic=topics[post.topic], body_html=markdown.to_html(post.body))\n    for page in pages:\n        _write(env, out, page_path(page), \"public/page.html\", page=page,\n               body_html=markdown.to_html(page.body))\n    with conn:\n        conn.execute(\"INSERT INTO site_state (id, last_export_at) VALUES (1, ?)\"\n                     \" ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_export_at = excluded.last_export_at\",\n                     (db.now(),))\n    return len(posts)\n\n\ndef last_export(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"When the public site was last exported, or None if it never was.\"\"\"\n    row = conn.execute(\"SELECT last_export_at FROM site_state\").fetchone()\n    return row[\"last_export_at\"] if row else None\n\n\ndef _environment(topics: list[TopicPage], menu: list[Page]) -> Environment:\n    \"\"\"Templates for every exported file: the site title, the published pages for\n    the menu (in menu order), and the topics for the row beneath it.\"\"\"\n    env = Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n                      autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]))\n    env.filters[\"spanish_date\"] = spanish_date\n    env.globals.update(site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE, post_path=post_path,\n                       page_path=page_path, menu=menu, topics=topics)\n    return env\n\n\ndef _write(env: Environment, out: Path, path: str, template: str, **context: Any) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Render one page to `out / path`. Its links go through href(), which turns a\n    path from the site root into one relative to this page, percent-encoded.\"\"\"\n    up = \"../\" * path.count(\"/\")\n\n    def href(target: str) -> str:\n        return up + quote(target)\n\n    file = out / path\n    file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    file.write_text(env.get_template(template).render(href=href, **context), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n----\n=== templates/public/_cerro_de_la_silla.html\n{# The home page's banner: the Cerro de la Silla over the city, drawn for this site.\n   The scene is wide and the peaks sit low, so a wide screen crops only sky and\n   foothills. where it is written, from the site root: \"tema/alineación.html\"\n    posts: list[Post]\n\n\ndef post_path(post: Post) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Where a post's page is written, from the site root.\"\"\"\n    return f\"posts/{post.slug}.html\"\n\n\ndef page_path(page: Page) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Where a page is written: at the site root, beside the home page.\"\"\"\n    return f\"{page.slug}.html\"\n\n\ndef export_site(conn: sqlite3.Connection, out: Path) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Wipe `out`, write the public site into it, and record when; returns how many\n    posts it holds.\"\"\"\n    posts = content.published_posts(conn)\n    pages = content.published_pages(conn)\n    topics = {key: TopicPage(name, f\"tema/{content.slugify(name)}.html\",\n                             [post for post in posts if post.topic == key])\n              for key, name in content.TOPICS.items()}\n\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    shutil.copyfile(settings.TEMPLATES / \"public\" / \"style.css\", out / \"style.css\")\n    env = _environment(list(topics.values()), pages)\n    _write(env, out, \"index.html\", \"public/home.html\")\n    for topic in topics.values():  # Its links go through href(), which turns a\n    path from the site root into one relative to this page, percent-encoded.\"\"\"\n    up = \"../\" * path.count(\"/\")\n\n    def href(target: str) -> str:\n        return up + quote(target)\n\n    file = out / path\n    file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    file.write_text(env.get_template(template).render(href=href, **context), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n----\n=== templates/public/_cerro_de_la_silla.html\n{# The home page's banner: the Cerro de la Silla over the city, drawn for this site.\n   The scene is wide and the peaks sit low, so a wide screen crops only sky and\n   foothills. Solid fills only, so it needs no image file and no pattern. #}\n<svg class=\"banner\" viewBox=\"0 0 2400 300\" preserveAspectRatio=\"xMidYMax slice\"\n     role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Cerro de la ry=\"14\"/><ellipse cx=\"2120\" cy=\"110\" rx=\"64\" ry=\"14\"/>\n  </g>\n  {# The far sierra, paler, behind the Cerro. #}\n  <path fill=\"#b9c7e2\" d=\"M0 300V214C200 196 360 206 520 192S760 166 860 {"parentUuid":"87015e1a-de13-469a-ad77-dc95055da49c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c3efc2a3-52e0-4dbd-b89f-42ac058af50a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KSitsYVneYnzjpEPKJtCtQ","type":"tool_result","content":"/* The public site: navy and white, with rayas across the top of every page. */\n:root { --navy: #0b2a5b; --navy-soft: #e8edf6; --ink: #1a1a1a; --muted: #4a4a4a; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { margin: 0; font: 17px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--ink); background: #fff; }\na { color: var(--navy); }\n\n.stripes { height: 2.5rem; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--navy) 0 1.25rem, #fff 1.25rem 2.5rem); }\n.band { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: .25rem 1.5rem; padding: .75rem 1rem; background: var(--navy); color: #fff; }\n.band a { color: #fff; }\n.site-name { font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 800; text-decoration: none; }\n.menu, .topics { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .25rem 1rem; }\n.topics { padding: .5rem 1rem; background: var(--navy-soft); border-bottom: 3px solid var(--navy); }\n.topics a { font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }\n\nmain { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 1rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\nh1, h2 { color: var(--navy); line-height: 1.2; }\n.meta { margin: .25rem 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: .9rem; }\n.posts { padding: 0; list-style: none; }\n.posts li { padding: .5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--navy-soft); }\n.body pre { overflow-x: auto; padding: .5rem; background: var(--navy-soft); }\n.body blockquote { margin-left: 0; padding-left: 1rem; border-left: 4px solid var(--navy); }\n\n/* The drawings are inline SVG. The banner keeps a phone-friendly height and crops\n   its sky or sides to fill the width; the stadium shrinks with the screen. */\n.banner { display: block; width: 100%; height: clamp(7rem, 22vw, 15rem); }\n.stadium { display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 20rem; height: auto; margin: 0 auto .75rem; }\n\nfooter { margin-top: 2rem; padding: 1rem; background: var(--navy); color: #fff; text-align: center; }\n.disclaimer { margin: 0; }\n.disclaimer[lang=\"en\"] { font-size: .85rem; opacity: .85; }\n----\n\"\"\"T08 (#9): the public site's final look, drawn inline with no image files.\n\nEach test name says which acceptance criterion of #9 it covers. {"parentUuid":"27558a16-cecc-45cb-b0d8-1a0d5fea4eb4","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c3efc2a3-52e0-4dbd-b89f-42ac058af50a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"0f72366a-5a8d-4096-80d4-2648356c39bc","timestamp":"2026-10-15T20:00:05.683Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_019htSUGR6Qz9C55dgihZtr1","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

test_home_has_a_section_per_topic_in_fixed_order_with_three_newest_and_ver_todos_hiding_empty_topics(\n        published_post, client_as, write_post, export):\n    for day in (1, 2, 3, 4):\n        published_post(day=day, title=f\"Crónica de la jornada {day}\", topic=\"match\")\n    published_post(day=5, title=\"Al técnico hay que darle tiempo\",  # newest of all, but Técnico comes second\n                   topic=\"coach\")\n    published_post(by=\"admin\", day=2, title=\"Watch party del Clásico\", topic=\"fan-club-news\")\n    write_post(client_as(\"editor\"), title=\"Un borrador de alineación\", topic=\"lineup\")  # never published\n\n    home = (export() / \"index.html\").read_text()\n\n    found = sections(home)\n    assert [text(inside(s, \"h2\")) for s in found] == [\n        \"Partido\", \"Técnico\", \"Noticias del club de aficionados\"]\n    match = found[0]\n    assert list_items(match) == [\n        \"Crónica de la jornada 4 Rayada de Corazón · 4 de octubre de 2026\",\n        \"Crónica de la jornada 3 Rayada de Corazón · 3 de octubre de 2026\",\n        \"Crónica de la jornada 2 Rayada de Corazón · 2 de octubre de 2026\",\n    ]\n    assert links(match)[\"Crónica de la jornada 4\"] == \"posts/cr%C3%B3nica-de-la-jornada-4.html\"\n    assert links(match)[\"Ver todos\"] == \"tema/partido.html\"\n    assert links(found[2])[\"Ver todos\"] == \"tema/noticias-del-club-de-aficionados.html\"\n    assert \"El Capi\" in list_items(found[2])[0]\n\n\ndef test_home_with_nothing_published_says_so(export):\n    home = (export() / \"index.html\").read_text()\n\n    assert sections(home) == []\n    assert \"Todavía no hay publicaciones.\" in home\n\n\ndef test_every_href_and_src_is_relative_percent_encoded_and_resolves_to_a_generated_file(\n        published_post, export):\n    published_post(title=\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\", topic=\"lineup\",\n                   body=\"Más en [la liga](https://example.com/liga).\")\n    published_post(title=\"Año de la Pandilla\", topic=\"signings\")\n    site = export()\n\n    checked = set()\n    for path, html in every_file_in(site).items():\n        for link in re.findall(r'(?:href|src)=\"([^\"]*)\"', html):\n            assert not link.startswith(\"/\"), f\"root-absolute {link} in {path}\"\n            assert link.isascii(), f\"{link} in {path} is not percent-encoded\"\n            if re.match(r\"(https?|mailto):\", link):\n                continue\n            target = ((site / path).parent / unquote(link)).resolve()\n            assert target.is_file(), f\"{link} in {path} leads nowhere\"\n            assert target.is_relative_to(site.resolve())\n            checked.add(link)\n\n    assert \"../posts/cr%C3%B3nica-del-cl%C3%A1sico-regio.html\" in checked\n    assert \"posts/a%C3%B1o-de-la-pandilla.html\" in checked\n    assert \"tema/alineaci%C3%B3n.html\" in checked\n\n\ndef test_every_public_page_has_the_striped_header_menu_with_inicio_topic_links_and_the_disclaimer(\n        published_post, export):\n    published_post(title=\"Crónica del Clásico Regio\")\n    files = every_file_in(export())\n\n    stripes = re.search(r\"\\.stripes\\s*\\{[^}]*\\}\", files[\"style.css\"])\n    assert stripes and \"repeating-linear-gradient\" in stripes.group(0)\n    assert \"var(--navy)\" in stripes.group(0) and \"#fff\" in stripes.group(0)\n    pages = {path: html for path, html in files.items() if path.endswith(\".html\")}\n    assert len(pages) == 1 + 5 + 1  # home, the five topic pages, the post\n    for path, html in pages.items():\n        header = inside(html, \"header\")\n        assert 'class=\"stripes\"' in header, path\n        menu = re.search(r'<nav class=\"menu\"[^>]*>(.*?)</nav>', header, re.S).group(1)\n        assert \"Inicio\" in links(menu), path\n        topics = re.search(r'<nav class=\"topics\"[^>]*>(.*?)</nav>', header, re.S).group(1)\n        assert list(links(topics)) == [\"Partido\", \"Alineación\", \"Técnico\", \"Fichajes\",\n                                       \"Noticias del club de aficionados\"], path\n        assert text(inside(html, \"footer\")) == (\n            \"Sitio de aficionados. Sin afiliación con el Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"\n            \" Fan site, not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey.\"), A page's scene is\nthe inline <svg> carrying data-scene=\"<name>\". The motion (scroll-driven, played\nonce on load, still under reduced motion), readability over the scenes and the\n390 px layout are checked by hand in a browser.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\n\ndef inside(html: str, tag: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The HTML inside the page's first <tag>.\"\"\"\n    match = re.search(rf\"<{tag}[^>]*>(.*?)</{tag}>\", html, re.S)\n    assert match, f\"no <{tag}>\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef text(html: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"What a reader sees of this HTML: tags dropped, spaces collapsed.\"\"\"\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", re.sub(r\"<[^>]+>\", \" \", html)).strip()\n\n\ndef scenes(html: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The name of each scene drawn on the page, in order.\"\"\"\n    return re.findall(r'<svg\\b[^>]*\\bdata-scene=\"([^\"]+)\"', html)\n\n\ndef test_home_page_carries_the_goal_scene_and_a_caption_naming_the_moment_inviting_a_scroll(\n        export):\n    home = (export() / {"parentUuid":"624c6a2c-f2ad-4d0d-b603-5b99acf6ff43","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/templates/public/style.css","snippet":"7\t.stripes { height: 2.5rem; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--navy) 0 1.25rem, #fff 1.25rem 2.5rem); }\n8\t.band { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: .25rem 1.5rem; padding: .75rem 1rem; background: var(--navy); color: #fff; }\n9\t.band a { color: #fff; }\n10\t.site-name { font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 800; text-decoration: none; }\n11\t.menu, .topics { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .25rem 1rem; }\n12\t.topics { padding: .5rem 1rem; background: var(--navy-soft); border-bottom: 3px solid var(--navy); }\n13\t.topics a { font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }\n14\t\n15\tmain { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: clamp(2.5rem, 16vh, 9rem) 1rem 1rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n16\th1, h2 { color: var(--navy); line-height: 1.2; }\n17\t.meta { margin: .25rem 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: .9rem; }\n18\t.posts { padding: 0; list-style: none; }\n19\t.posts li { padding: .5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--navy-soft); }\n20\t.body pre { overflow-x: auto; padding: .5rem; background: var(--navy-soft); }\n21\t.body blockquote { margin-left: 0; padding-left: 1rem; border-left: 4px solid var(--navy); }\n22\t\n23\t/* The drawings are inline SVG.
