{"parentUuid":"7151cb89-7284-4c12-ac44-e0c51c6bbb6b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4o2WvZsrBvsjQk3Ndw7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017pCqCKokWm3vCpFEosBTuV","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/templates/public/scenes/goal.html","content":"{# Inicio: Suazo's goal in the 90th minute of the Apertura 2009 final (Cruz Azul 1–2\n   Rayados, 13 Dec 2009), seen from above, like a broadcast's aerial camera over the\n   Cruz Azul box. Drawn for this site: tokens and markings, no crests or real faces.\n\n   The markup is the FINAL frame (1–2 and FINAL on the score bar, the ball in the net,\n   the team round the 26 and the cup held up to the camera), so with reduced motion,\n   or a page too short to scroll, that is what shows. Every .beat runs on one story\n   clock, 0% to 100%: the scroll through the goal story (.story in home.html, which\n   spaces its captions to these beats) where the browser supports scroll-driven\n   animation, otherwise 10 s from load, once.\n      0–36  the 26 dribbles in, his run drawn behind him; the camera pushes in\n     36–41  the shot, its arc drawn to the far corner; the keeper dives the other way\n     41–48  the net bulges, a flash, the camera shakes; 1–1 turns 1–2\n     44–70  he wheels away and the team piles on; confetti falls; 90' turns FINAL\n     82–92  the cup goes up to the camera; CAMPEÓN\n   Movers carry their place as a CSS transform (translate, then rotate), never as a\n   transform attribute. The key action stays inside x 580–1020, y 180–820, which a\n   phone in portrait still shows once the scene is cropped to fill the screen. #}\n{% from \"public/scenes/_parts.html\" import scene %}\n\n{# A player seen from above, facing up, centred on (0, 0): his shadow, boots that\n   stride on the story clock (stride names the keyframes; \"\" stands still),\n   shoulders in his kit (\"rayados\" or a colour), then his head. #}\n{% macro player(kit, stride=\"\") -%}\n  <ellipse cx=\"6\" cy=\"9\" rx=\"21\" ry=\"13\" fill=\"#0b1f12\" opacity=\".22\"/>\n  <g fill=\"#14181f\">\n    <ellipse {% if stride %}class=\"{{ stride }}-a beat\" {% endif %}cx=\"-7\" rx=\"5\" ry=\"7\"/>\n    <ellipse {% if stride %}class=\"{{ stride }}-b beat\" {% endif %}cx=\"7\" rx=\"5\" ry=\"7\"/>\n  </g>\n  {% if kit == \"rayados\" %}\n  <rect x=\"-19\" y=\"-9\" width=\"38\" height=\"18\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#fff\" stroke=\"#0b2a5b\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n  <g fill=\"#0b2a5b\">\n    <rect x=\"-11\" y=\"-8\" width=\"5\" height=\"16\"/><rect x=\"-2.5\" y=\"-9\" width=\"5\" height=\"18\"/>\n    <rect x=\"6\" y=\"-8\" width=\"5\" height=\"16\"/>\n  </g>\n  {% else %}\n  <rect x=\"-19\" y=\"-9\" width=\"38\" height=\"18\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"{{ kit }}\" stroke=\"#0b1f45\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n  {% endif %}\n  <circle r=\"8.5\" fill=\"#8d5b3a\"/>\n  <circle cy=\"2\" r=\"7.5\" fill=\"#1d130c\"/>\n{%- endmacro %}\n\n{# Boots that stride: within each [start, end) span of the story, every 3% the\n   foot swaps between forward and back; outside the spans it rests. #}\n{% macro strides(name, first, second, spans) -%}\n  @keyframes {{ name }} {\n    {%- for start, end in spans %}\n    {% if start > 0 %}{{ start - 1 }}% { transform: none; }{% endif %}\n    {%- for t in range(start, end, 3) %}\n    {{ t }}% { transform: translateY({{ first if loop.index0 % 2 == 0 else second }}px); }\n    {%- endfor %}\n    {{ end }}% { transform: none; }\n    {%- endfor %}\n    to { transform: none; } }\n{%- endmacro %}\n\n{% call scene(\"goal\") %}\n  <style>\n    .story { view-timeline: --story block; }\n    .scene-goal .beat { animation-duration: 10s; animation-timing-function: linear;\n                        animation-fill-mode: both; }\n    @supports (animation-timeline: view()) {\n      .scene-goal .beat { animation-duration: auto; animation-timeline: --story;\n                          animation-range: contain; }\n    }\n    .scene-goal .centre { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 50%; }\n\n    /* The camera: it starts high, pushes in on the box, shakes at the goal, and\n       pulls back out for the celebration. */\n    .goal-cam { transform-origin: 800px 330px; animation-name: goal-cam; }\n    @keyframes goal-cam {\n      from { transform: scale(.92) translate(0, 0); animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; }\n      30% { transform: scale(1.16) translate(0, 0); }\n      40% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(0, 0); }\n      41.5% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(5px, -4px); }\n      42.5% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(-5px, 4px); }\n      43.5% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(3px, -2px); }\n      45% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(0, 0); animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; }\n      62% { transform: scale(1.08) translate(0, 0); }\n      to { transform: scale(1) translate(0, 0); } }\n\n    {{ strides(\"goal-run-a\", -8, 6, [(0, 36), (46, 66)]) }}\n    {{ strides(\"goal-run-b\", 6, -8, [(0, 36), (46, 66)]) }}\n    {{ strides(\"goal-chase-a\", -8, 6, [(0, 40)]) }}\n    {{ strides(\"goal-chase-b\", 6, -8, [(0, 40)]) }}\n    .goal-run-a { animation-name: goal-run-a; } .goal-run-b { animation-name: goal-run-b; }\n    .goal-chase-a { animation-name: goal-chase-a; } .goal-chase-b { animation-name: goal-chase-b; }\n\n    /* The 26: his place, then (inside) which way he faces. */\n    .goal-suazo { transform: translate(930px, 625px); animation-name: goal-suazo; }\n    @keyframes goal-suazo {\n      from { transform: translate(985px, 860px); } 10% { transform: translate(960px, 760px); }\n      20% { transform: translate(925px, 660px); } 30% { transform: translate(885px, 560px); }\n      34% { transform: translate(858px, 480px); } 36% { transform: translate(848px, 448px); }\n      40% { transform: translate(846px, 442px); } 46% { transform: translate(868px, 500px); }\n      56% { transform: translate(920px, 610px); } 64%, to { transform: translate(930px, 625px); } }\n    .goal-suazo-turn { animation-name: goal-suazo-turn; }\n    @keyframes goal-suazo-turn {\n      from, 30% { transform: rotate(-14deg); } 34% { transform: rotate(-24deg); }\n      38% { transform: rotate(-28deg); } 44% { transform: rotate(150deg); }\n      58% { transform: rotate(160deg); } 66%, to { transform: none; } }\n    .goal-arms { animation-name: goal-arms; }\n    @keyframes goal-arms { from, 82% { opacity: 0; } 86%, to { opacity: 1; } }\n\n    .goal-ball { transform: translate(772px, 292px); animation-name: goal-ball; }\n    @keyframes goal-ball {\n      from { transform: translate(978px, 843px); } 10% { transform: translate(953px, 743px); }\n      20% { transform: translate(918px, 643px); } 30% { transform: translate(879px, 543px); }\n      34% { transform: translate(853px, 463px); }\n      36% { transform: translate(846px, 434px); animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .4, 1); }\n      41% { transform: translate(770px, 288px); } 44%, to { transform: translate(772px, 292px); } }\n    .goal-ball-air { animation-name: goal-ball-air; }\n    @keyframes goal-ball-air {\n      from, 36% { transform: none; } 38.5% { transform: translate(-4px, -10px) scale(1.45); }\n      41%, to { transform: none; } }\n    .goal-trail { stroke-dasharray: 100; animation-name: goal-trail; }\n    @keyframes goal-trail { from { stroke-dashoffset: 100; } 36%, to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }\n    .goal-shot { stroke-dasharray: 100; animation-name: goal-shot; }\n    @keyframes goal-shot { from, 36% { stroke-dashoffset: 100; } 41%, to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }\n\n    .goal-keeper { transform: translate(850px, 322px) rotate(90deg); animation-name: goal-keeper; }\n    @keyframes goal-keeper {\n      from { transform: translate(800px, 316px) rotate(180deg); }\n      30% { transform: translate(810px, 318px) rotate(180deg); }\n      38% { transform: translate(814px, 318px) rotate(180deg); }\n      41%, to { transform: translate(850px, 322px) rotate(90deg); } }\n    .goal-d1 { transform: translate(888px, 515px) rotate(-30deg); animation-name: goal-d1; }\n    @keyframes goal-d1 {\n      from { transform: translate(1035px, 830px) rotate(-25deg); }\n      30% { transform: translate(925px, 610px) rotate(-25deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(895px, 520px) rotate(-20deg); }\n      44%, to { transform: translate(888px, 515px) rotate(-30deg); } }\n    .goal-d2 { transform: translate(822px, 468px) rotate(50deg); animation-name: goal-d2; }\n    @keyframes goal-d2 {\n      from { transform: translate(770px, 520px) rotate(0deg); }\n      30% { transform: translate(812px, 488px) rotate(20deg); }\n      36%, to { transform: translate(822px, 468px) rotate(50deg); } }\n    .goal-d3 { transform: translate(742px, 352px) rotate(70deg); animation-name: goal-d3; }\n    @keyframes goal-d3 {\n      from { transform: translate(690px, 400px) rotate(60deg); }\n      36%, to { transform: translate(742px, 352px) rotate(70deg); } }\n\n    /* His teammates: a decoy run each, then they pile on round him. */\n    .goal-t1 { transform: translate(892px, 622px) rotate(90deg); animation-name: goal-t1; }\n    @keyframes goal-t1 {\n      from { transform: translate(650px, 700px) rotate(10deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(705px, 440px) rotate(10deg); }\n      44% { transform: translate(720px, 450px) rotate(100deg); }\n      58%, to { transform: translate(892px, 622px) rotate(90deg); } }\n    .goal-t2 { transform: translate(906px, 592px) rotate(144deg); animation-name: goal-t2; }\n    @keyframes goal-t2 {\n      from { transform: translate(830px, 900px) rotate(-5deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(790px, 640px) rotate(-5deg); }\n      46% { transform: translate(800px, 650px) rotate(60deg); }\n      62%, to { transform: translate(906px, 592px) rotate(144deg); } }\n    .goal-t3 { transform: translate(968px, 622px) rotate(-90deg); animation-name: goal-t3; }\n    @keyframes goal-t3 {\n      from { transform: translate(1100px, 700px) rotate(-20deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(1060px, 610px) rotate(-20deg); }\n      46% { transform: translate(1050px, 600px) rotate(-90deg); }\n      62%, to { transform: translate(968px, 622px) rotate(-90deg); } }\n    .goal-t4 { transform: translate(954px, 592px) rotate(216deg); animation-name: goal-t4; }\n    @keyframes goal-t4 {\n      from { transform: translate(720px, 860px) rotate(15deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(760px, 700px) rotate(15deg); }\n      46% { transform: translate(770px, 690px) rotate(45deg); }\n      64%, to { transform: translate(954px, 592px) rotate(216deg); } }\n\n    /* The goal: the net bulges, a ring spreads from the ball, the screen flashes. */\n    .goal-net { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 100%; animation-name: goal-net; }\n    @keyframes goal-net {\n      from, 40.5% { transform: none; } 41.5% { transform: scale(1.08, 1.7); }\n      43% { transform: scale(.98, .8); } 44.5% { transform: scale(1.02, 1.25); }\n      46% { transform: scale(1, .92); } 48%, to { transform: none; } }\n    .goal-ripple { opacity: 0; animation-name: goal-ripple; }\n    @keyframes goal-ripple {\n      from, 40.5% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(.3); } 41% { opacity: 1; }\n      47%, to { opacity: 0; transform: scale(3.2); } }\n    .goal-flash { opacity: 0; animation-name: goal-flash; }\n    @keyframes goal-flash { from, 40.5% { opacity: 0; } 41.5% { opacity: .5; } 45%, to { opacity: 0; } }\n\n    /* The cup goes up to the camera: bigger, and its shadow further off. */\n    .goal-cup { transform: translate(930px, 586px) scale(1.15); animation-name: goal-cup; }\n    @keyframes goal-cup {\n      from, 82% { opacity: 0; transform: translate(930px, 616px) scale(.5); }\n      86% { opacity: 1; } 92%, to { opacity: 1; transform: translate(930px, 586px) scale(1.15); } }\n    .goal-cup-shadow { transform: translate(952px, 624px) scale(1.15); animation-name: goal-cup-shadow; }\n    @keyframes goal-cup-shadow {\n      from, 82% { opacity: 0; transform: translate(932px, 620px) scale(.5); }\n      86% { opacity: 1; } 92%, to { opacity: 1; transform: translate(952px, 624px) scale(1.15); } }\n\n    /* Confetti falls toward the pitch: each layer starts near the camera, big, and\n       settles. */\n    .goal-fall-1, .goal-fall-2, .goal-fall-3 { transform-origin: 800px 500px; }\n    .goal-fall-1 { animation-name: goal-fall-1; }\n    @keyframes goal-fall-1 { from, 46% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(2.2); } 50% { opacity: 1; }\n                             68%, to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }\n    .goal-fall-2 { animation-name: goal-fall-2; }\n    @keyframes goal-fall-2 { from, 52% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(2.2); } 56% { opacity: 1; }\n                             76%, to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }\n    .goal-fall-3 { animation-name: goal-fall-3; }\n    @keyframes goal-fall-3 { from, 58% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(2.2); } 62% { opacity: 1; }\n                             86%, to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }\n\n    /* The score bar: 1 slides out and 2 in, the Rayados side flashes gold, 90' turns\n       FINAL, and CAMPEÓN drops in under it. */\n    .goal-was { opacity: 0; animation-name: goal-was; }\n    @keyframes goal-was { from, 41% { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n                          43%, to { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-18px); } }\n    .goal-now { animation-name: goal-now; }\n    @keyframes goal-now { from, 41% { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px); }\n                          44%, to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }\n    .goal-gold { opacity: 0; animation-name: goal-gold; }\n    @keyframes goal-gold { from, 41% { opacity: 0; } 43% { opacity: .9; } 46% { opacity: .2; }\n                           49% { opacity: .9; } 54%, to { opacity: 0; } }\n    .goal-minute { opacity: 0; animation-name: goal-minute; }\n    @keyframes goal-minute { from, 70% { opacity: 1; } 72%, to { opacity: 0; } }\n    .goal-final { animation-name: goal-final; }\n    @keyframes goal-final { from, 70% { opacity: 0; } 72%, to { opacity: 1; } }\n    .goal-champ { animation-name: goal-champ; }\n    @keyframes goal-champ { from, 84% { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-12px); }\n                            90%, to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }\n\n    /* Always on, whatever the story: the stands jump, the confetti flutters, the\n       cup shines. */\n    .goal-fans { animation: goal-jump 1.4s ease-in-out infinite alternate; }\n    @keyframes goal-jump { to { stroke-width: 13.5; } }\n    .goal-confetti rect { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 50%;\n                          transform: rotate(var(--r));\n                          animation: goal-flutter 1.1s ease-in-out infinite alternate; }\n    @keyframes goal-flutter { from { transform: rotate(var(--r)); }\n                              to { transform: rotate(var(--r)) scaleX(.15); } }\n    .goal-shine { animation: goal-shine 1.2s ease-in-out infinite alternate; }\n    @keyframes goal-shine { from { opacity: .15; } to { opacity: 1; } }\n  </style>\n\n  <g class=\"goal-cam beat\">\n    {# The stands round three sides, the crowd as heads seen from above: each row\n       or column is three dotted lines, one per colour. Then the boards. #}\n    <rect width=\"1600\" height=\"1000\" fill=\"#9aa7bd\"/>\n    {% set heads = [\"#2f6fd1\", \"#eef2f8\", \"#1b2235\"] %}\n    <g stroke-width=\"11\" stroke-linecap=\"round\">\n stroke-dasharray=\"0 42\" stroke-dashoffset=\"-{{ (k % 2) * 7 + c * 14 }}\"\n            style=\"animation-delay: -{{ (k * 0.13) | round(2) }}s\"/>\n      {% endfor %}{% endfor %}\n      {% for k in </g>\n    {# The Rayados fans' block, in the far stand. #}\n    <rect x=\"1276\" y=\"372\" width=\"148\" height=\"276\" fill=\"#9aa7bd\"/>\n    <g stroke-width=\"11\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-dasharray=\"0 28\">\n      {% for x in range(1284, 1424, 20) %}\n      <line class=\"goal-fans\" x1=\"{{ x }}\" y1=\"380\" x2=\"{{ x }}\" y2=\"640\" stroke=\"#0b2a5b\"/>\n      <line pitch, mown in bands, and the markings of the attacking half. #}\n    <rect x=\"460\" y=\"300\" width=\"680\" height=\"700\" fill=\"#3f8f4a\"/>\n    <g fill=\"#469a52\">{% for y in range(360, 1000, <circle cx=\"-22\" cy=\"-6\" r=\"5\" fill=\"#fff\" stroke=\"#14181f\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/>\n      <circle cx=\"22\" cy=\"-6\" r=\"5\" fill=\"#fff\" stroke=\"#14181f\" stroke-width=\"1.5\"/>\n    </g>\n    <g class=\"goal-d1 beat\">{{ player(\"#2f6fd1\", \"goal-chase\") }}</g>\n    <g class=\"goal-d2 beat\">{{ player(\"#2f6fd1\", \"goal-chase\") }}</g>\n    <g class=\"goal-d3 beat\">{{ beat\">{{ player(\"rayados\", \"goal-run\") }}</g>\n    <g class=\"goal-t4 beat\">{{ player(\"rayados\", \"goal-run\") }}</g>\n\n    {# The ball, with its shadow on the grass: in the air it grows and broadcast; at the end, arms up to the cup. #}\n    <g class=\"goal-suazo beat\">\n      <g class=\"goal-suazo-turn beat\">\n        {{ player(\"rayados\", \"goal-run\") }}\n        <g class=\"goal-arms beat\" stroke=\"#8d5b3a\" stroke-width=\"6\" stroke-linecap=\"round\">\n          <line x1=\"-15\" y1=\"-3\" x2=\"-6\" y2=\"-34\"/><line x1=\"15\" y1=\"-3\" x2=\"6\" y2=\"-34\"/>\n        </g>\n      </g>\n      <g transform=\"translate(0 38)\">\n        <path d=\"M-6-12h12l-6-7z\" fill=\"#fff\"/>\n        <rect x=\"-50\" y=\"-12\" width=\"100\" height=\"24\" rx=\"6\" fill=\"#fff\"/>\n        <text y=\"6\" font-family=\"system-ui, sans-serif\" font-size=\"15\" font-weight=\"800\"\n              text-anchor=\"middle\" fill=\"#0b2a5b\">26 · SUAZO</text>\n      </g>\n    </g>\n\n    <circle class=\"goal-ripple beat centre\" cx=\"770\" cy=\"290\" r=\"14\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"#fff\" stroke-width=\"4\"/>\n    {# The roof's shadow across the stand and a corner of the pitch. #}\n    <path d=\"M0 0H1600V110L0 440Z\" fill=\"#000\" opacity=\".12\"/>\n\n    {# The cup, from above: rim, bowl, handles and a shine. #}\n    <g class=\"goal-cup beat\">\n      <g fill=\"none\" stroke=\"#c9961f\" stroke-width=\"4\">\n        <ellipse cx=\"-20\" rx=\"7\" ry=\"9\"/><ellipse cx=\"20\" rx=\"7\" ry=\"9\"/>\n      </g>\n      <circle r=\"18\" fill=\"#f0c445\" stroke=\"#a87b14\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n      <circle r=\"12.5\" fill=\"#c9961f\"/>\n      <path d=\"M-11-6a12.5 12.5 0 0 1 9-7\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"#fff\" stroke-width=\"3\"\n            stroke-linecap=\"round\" opacity=\".7\"/>\n      <g class=\"goal-shine\" fill=\"#f0c445\">\n        <path d=\"M-30-24l3 7 7 3-7 3-3 7-3-7-7-3 7-3z\"/><path d=\"M28-20l2 5 5 2-5 2-2 5-2-5-5-2 5-2z\"/>\n      </g>\n    </g>\n  </g>\n\n  {# Confetti, in three layers, over the camera; none on the score bar. #}\n  {% set papers = [\"#0b2a5b\", \"#3d6fb6\", \"#e5b53a\", \"#ffffff\"] %}\n  {% for layer in range(3) %}\n  <g class=\"goal-fall-{{ layer + 1 }} beat\">\n    <g class=\"goal-confetti\" stroke=\"#0b2a5b\" stroke-width=\"1.5\">\n      {% for i in range(layer, 63, 3) %}\n      {% set x = (i * 293 + 47) % 1600 %}{% set y = 30 + (i * 157) % 940 %}{% set r = (i * 67) % 180 %}\n      {% if not (560 < x < 1040 and 140 < y < 280) %}\n      <rect x=\"{{ x }}\" y=\"{{ y }}\" width=\"10\" height=\"17\" rx=\"2\" fill=\"{{ papers[i % 4] }}\"\n            style=\"--r: {{ r }}deg; animation-delay: -{{ ((i % 7) * 0.2) | round(2) }}s\"/>\n      {% endif %}\n      {% endfor %}\n    </g>\n  </g>\n  {% endfor %}\n\n  {# The score bar, like a broadcast's. #}\n  <g font-family=\"system-ui, sans-serif\" font-weight=\"800\">\n    <rect x=\"580\" y=\"166\" width=\"440\" height=\"46\" rx=\"8\" fill=\"#061d42\"/>\n    <rect class=\"goal-gold beat\" x=\"865\" y=\"166\" width=\"155\" height=\"46\" rx=\"8\" fill=\"#e5b53a\"/>\n    <rect x=\"735\" y=\"166\" width=\"130\" height=\"46\" fill=\"#0b2a5b\"/>\n    <rect x=\"588\" y=\"174\" width=\"7\" height=\"30\" rx=\"2\" fill=\"#2f6fd1\"/>\n    <rect x=\"1005\" y=\"174\" width=\"7\" height=\"30\" rx=\"2\" fill=\"#fff\"/>\n    <rect x=\"1007.5\" y=\"174\" width=\"2\" height=\"30\" fill=\"#0b2a5b\"/>\n    <g font-size=\"19\" fill=\"#fff\">\n      <text x=\"604\" y=\"196\">CRUZ AZUL</text><text x=\"996\" y=\"196\" text-anchor=\"end\">RAYADOS</text>\n    </g>\n    <g font-size=\"30\" font-weight=\"900\" fill=\"#fff\" text-anchor=\"middle\">\n      <text x=\"768\" y=\"200\">1</text><text x=\"800\" y=\"198\">–</text>\n      <text class=\"goal-was beat\" x=\"832\" y=\"200\">1</text>\n      <text class=\"goal-now beat\" x=\"832\" y=\"200\">2</text>\n    </g>\n    <g class=\"goal-minute beat\">\n Inicio: Suazo's goal in the 90th minute of the Apertura 2009 final (Cruz Azul 1–2\n   Rayados, 13 Dec 2009), seen from above, like a broadcast's aerial camera over the\n   Cruz Azul box. Drawn for this site: tokens and markings, no crests or real faces.\n\n   The markup is the FINAL frame (1–2 and FINAL on the score bar, the ball in the net,\n   the team round the 26 and the cup held up to the camera), so with reduced motion,\n   or a page too short to scroll, that is what shows. Every .beat runs on one story\n   clock, 0% to 100%: the scroll through the goal story (.story in home.html, which\n   spaces its captions to these beats) where the browser supports scroll-driven\n   animation, otherwise 10 s from load, once.\n      0–36  the 26 dribbles in, his run drawn behind him; the camera pushes in\n     36–41  the shot, its arc drawn to the far corner; the keeper dives the other way\n     41–48  the net bulges, a flash, the camera shakes; 1–1 turns 1–2\n     44–70  he wheels away and the team piles on; confetti falls; 90' turns FINAL\n     82–92  the cup goes up to the camera; CAMPEÓN\n   Movers carry their place as a CSS transform (translate, then rotate), never as a\n   transform attribute. The key action stays inside x 580–1020, y 180–820, which a\n   phone in portrait still shows once the scene is cropped to fill the screen. #}\n{% from \"public/scenes/_parts.html\" import scene %}\n\n{# A player seen from above, facing up, centred on (0, 0): his shadow, boots that\n   stride on the story clock (stride names the keyframes; \"\" stands still),\n   shoulders in his kit (\"rayados\" or a colour), then his head. #}\n{% macro player(kit, stride=\"\") -%}\n  <ellipse cx=\"6\" cy=\"9\" rx=\"21\" ry=\"13\" fill=\"#0b1f12\" opacity=\".22\"/>\n  <g fill=\"#14181f\">\n    <ellipse {% if stride %}class=\"{{ stride }}-a beat\" {% endif %}cx=\"-7\" rx=\"5\" ry=\"7\"/>\n    <ellipse {% if stride %}class=\"{{ stride }}-b beat\" {% endif %}cx=\"7\" rx=\"5\" ry=\"7\"/>\n  </g>\n  {% if kit == \"rayados\" %}\n  <rect x=\"-19\" y=\"-9\" width=\"38\" height=\"18\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#fff\" stroke=\"#0b2a5b\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n  <g fill=\"#0b2a5b\">\n    <rect x=\"-11\" y=\"-8\" width=\"5\" height=\"16\"/><rect x=\"-2.5\" y=\"-9\" width=\"5\" height=\"18\"/>\n    <rect x=\"6\" y=\"-8\" width=\"5\" height=\"16\"/>\n  </g>\n  {% else %}\n  <rect x=\"-19\" y=\"-9\" width=\"38\" height=\"18\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"{{ kit }}\" stroke=\"#0b1f45\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n  {% endif %}\n  <circle r=\"8.5\" fill=\"#8d5b3a\"/>\n  <circle cy=\"2\" r=\"7.5\" fill=\"#1d130c\"/>\n{%- endmacro %}\n\n{# Boots that stride: within each [start, end) span of the story, every 3% the\n   foot swaps between forward and back; outside the spans it rests. #}\n{% macro strides(name, first, second, spans) -%}\n  @keyframes {{ name }} {\n    {%- for start, end in spans %}\n    {% if start > 0 %}{{ start - 1 }}% { transform: none; }{% endif %}\n    {%- for t in range(start, end, 3) %}\n    {{ t }}% { transform: translateY({{ first if loop.index0 % 2 == 0 else second }}px); }\n    {%- endfor %}\n    {{ end }}% { transform: none; }\n    {%- endfor %}\n    to { transform: none; } }\n{%- endmacro %}\n\n{% call scene(\"goal\") %}\n  <style>\n    .story { view-timeline: --story block; }\n    .scene-goal .beat { animation-duration: 10s; animation-timing-function: linear;\n                        animation-fill-mode: both; }\n    @supports (animation-timeline: view()) {\n      .scene-goal .beat { animation-duration: auto; animation-timeline: --story;\n                          animation-range: contain; }\n    }\n    .scene-goal .centre { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 50%; }\n\n    /* The camera: it starts high, pushes in on the box, shakes at the goal, and\n       pulls back out for the celebration. */\n    .goal-cam { transform-origin: 800px 330px; animation-name: goal-cam; }\n    @keyframes goal-cam {\n      from { transform: scale(.92) translate(0, 0); animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; }\n      30% { transform: scale(1.16) translate(0, 0); }\n      40% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(0, 0); }\n      41.5% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(5px, -4px); }\n      42.5% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(-5px, 4px); }\n      43.5% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(3px, -2px); }\n      45% { transform: scale(1.28) translate(0, 0); animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; }\n      62% { transform: scale(1.08) translate(0, 0); }\n      to { transform: scale(1) translate(0, 0); } }\n\n    {{ strides(\"goal-run-a\", -8, 6, [(0, 36), (46, 66)]) }}\n    {{ strides(\"goal-run-b\", 6, -8, [(0, 36), (46, 66)]) }}\n    {{ strides(\"goal-chase-a\", -8, 6, [(0, 40)]) }}\n    {{ strides(\"goal-chase-b\", 6, -8, [(0, 40)]) }}\n    .goal-run-a { animation-name: goal-run-a; } .goal-run-b { animation-name: goal-run-b; }\n    .goal-chase-a { animation-name: goal-chase-a; } .goal-chase-b { animation-name: goal-chase-b; }\n\n    /* The 26: his place, then (inside) which way he faces. */\n    .goal-suazo { transform: translate(930px, 625px); animation-name: goal-suazo; }\n    @keyframes goal-suazo {\n      from { transform: translate(985px, 860px); } 10% { transform: translate(960px, 760px); }\n      20% { transform: translate(925px, 660px); } 30% { transform: translate(885px, 560px); }\n      34% { transform: translate(858px, 480px); } 36% { transform: translate(848px, 448px); }\n      40% { transform: translate(846px, 442px); } 46% { transform: translate(868px, 500px); }\n      56% { transform: translate(920px, 610px); } 64%, to { transform: translate(930px, 625px); } }\n    .goal-suazo-turn { animation-name: goal-suazo-turn; }\n    @keyframes goal-suazo-turn {\n      from, 30% { transform: rotate(-14deg); } 34% { transform: rotate(-24deg); }\n      38% { transform: rotate(-28deg); } 44% { transform: rotate(150deg); }\n      58% { transform: rotate(160deg); } 66%, to { transform: none; } }\n    .goal-arms { animation-name: goal-arms; }\n    @keyframes goal-arms { from, 82% { opacity: 0; } 86%, to { opacity: 1; } }\n\n    .goal-ball { transform: translate(772px, 292px); animation-name: goal-ball; }\n    @keyframes goal-ball {\n      from { transform: translate(978px, 843px); } 10% { transform: translate(953px, 743px); }\n      20% { transform: translate(918px, 643px); } 30% { transform: translate(879px, 543px); }\n      34% { transform: translate(853px, 463px); }\n      36% { transform: translate(846px, 434px); animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .4, 1); }\n      41% { transform: translate(770px, 288px); } 44%, to { transform: translate(772px, 292px); } }\n    .goal-ball-air { animation-name: goal-ball-air; }\n    @keyframes goal-ball-air {\n      from, 36% { transform: none; } 38.5% { transform: translate(-4px, -10px) scale(1.45); }\n      41%, to { transform: none; } }\n    .goal-trail { stroke-dasharray: 100; animation-name: goal-trail; }\n    @keyframes goal-trail { from { stroke-dashoffset: 100; } 36%, to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }\n    .goal-shot { stroke-dasharray: 100; animation-name: goal-shot; }\n    @keyframes goal-shot { from, 36% { stroke-dashoffset: 100; } 41%, to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }\n\n    .goal-keeper { transform: translate(850px, 322px) rotate(90deg); animation-name: goal-keeper; }\n    @keyframes goal-keeper {\n      from { transform: translate(800px, 316px) rotate(180deg); }\n      30% { transform: translate(810px, 318px) rotate(180deg); }\n      38% { transform: translate(814px, 318px) rotate(180deg); }\n      41%, to { transform: translate(850px, 322px) rotate(90deg); } }\n    .goal-d1 { transform: translate(888px, 515px) rotate(-30deg); animation-name: goal-d1; }\n    @keyframes goal-d1 {\n      from { transform: translate(1035px, 830px) rotate(-25deg); }\n      30% { transform: translate(925px, 610px) rotate(-25deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(895px, 520px) rotate(-20deg); }\n      44%, to { transform: translate(888px, 515px) rotate(-30deg); } }\n    .goal-d2 { transform: translate(822px, 468px) rotate(50deg); animation-name: goal-d2; }\n    @keyframes goal-d2 {\n      from { transform: translate(770px, 520px) rotate(0deg); }\n      30% { transform: translate(812px, 488px) rotate(20deg); }\n      36%, to { transform: translate(822px, 468px) rotate(50deg); } }\n    .goal-d3 { transform: translate(742px, 352px) rotate(70deg); animation-name: goal-d3; }\n    @keyframes goal-d3 {\n      from { transform: translate(690px, 400px) rotate(60deg); }\n      36%, to { transform: translate(742px, 352px) rotate(70deg); } }\n\n    /* His teammates: a decoy run each, then they pile on round him. */\n    .goal-t1 { transform: translate(892px, 622px) rotate(90deg); animation-name: goal-t1; }\n    @keyframes goal-t1 {\n      from { transform: translate(650px, 700px) rotate(10deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(705px, 440px) rotate(10deg); }\n      44% { transform: translate(720px, 450px) rotate(100deg); }\n      58%, to { transform: translate(892px, 622px) rotate(90deg); } }\n    .goal-t2 { transform: translate(906px, 592px) rotate(144deg); animation-name: goal-t2; }\n    @keyframes goal-t2 {\n      from { transform: translate(830px, 900px) rotate(-5deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(790px, 640px) rotate(-5deg); }\n      46% { transform: translate(800px, 650px) rotate(60deg); }\n      62%, to { transform: translate(906px, 592px) rotate(144deg); } }\n    .goal-t3 { transform: translate(968px, 622px) rotate(-90deg); animation-name: goal-t3; }\n    @keyframes goal-t3 {\n      from { transform: translate(1100px, 700px) rotate(-20deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(1060px, 610px) rotate(-20deg); }\n      46% { transform: translate(1050px, 600px) rotate(-90deg); }\n      62%, to { transform: translate(968px, 622px) rotate(-90deg); } }\n    .goal-t4 { transform: translate(954px, 592px) rotate(216deg); animation-name: goal-t4; }\n    @keyframes goal-t4 {\n      from { transform: translate(720px, 860px) rotate(15deg); }\n      36% { transform: translate(760px, 700px) rotate(15deg); }\n      46% { transform: translate(770px, 690px) rotate(45deg); }\n      64%, to { transform: translate(954px, 592px) rotate(216deg); } }\n\n    /* The goal: the net bulges, a ring spreads from the ball, the screen flashes. */\n    .goal-net { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 100%; animation-name: goal-net; }\n    @keyframes goal-net {\n      from, 40.5% { transform: none; } 41.5% { transform: scale(1.08, 1.7); }\n      43% { transform: scale(.98, .8); } 44.5% { transform: scale(1.02, 1.25); }\n      46% { transform: scale(1, .92); } 48%, to { transform: none; } }\n    .goal-ripple { opacity: 0; Drawn for this site: tokens and markings, no crests or real faces.\n\n   The markup is the FINAL frame (1–2 and FINAL on the score bar, the ball in the net,\n   the team round the 26 and the cup held up to the camera), so with reduced motion,\n   or a page too short to scroll, that is what shows. Every .beat runs on one story\n   clock, 0% to 100%: the scroll through the goal story (.story in home.html, which\n   spaces its captions to these beats) where the browser supports scroll-driven\n   animation, otherwise 10 s from load, once.\n      0–36  the 26 dribbles in, his run drawn behind him; the camera pushes in\n     36–41  the shot, its arc drawn to the far corner; the keeper dives the other way\n     41–48  the net bulges, a flash, the camera shakes; 1–1 turns 1–2\n     44–70  he wheels away and the team piles on; confetti falls; 90' turns FINAL\n     82–92  the cup goes up to the camera; CAMPEÓN\n   Movers carry their place as a CSS transform (translate, then rotate), never as a\n   transform attribute. The key action stays inside x 580–1020, y 180–820, which a\n   phone in portrait still shows once the scene is cropped to fill the screen. #}\n{% from \"public/scenes/_parts.html\" import scene %}\n\n{# A player seen from above, facing up, centred on (0, 0): his shadow, boots that\n   stride on the story clock (stride names the keyframes; \"\" stands still),\n   shoulders in his kit (\"rayados\" or a colour), then his head. #}\n{% macro player(kit, stride=\"\") -%}\n  <ellipse cx=\"6\" cy=\"9\" rx=\"21\" ry=\"13\" fill=\"#0b1f12\" opacity=\".22\"/>\n  <g fill=\"#14181f\">\n    <ellipse {% if stride %}class=\"{{ stride }}-a beat\" {% endif %}cx=\"-7\" rx=\"5\" ry=\"7\"/>\n    <ellipse {% if stride %}class=\"{{ stride }}-b beat\" {% endif %}cx=\"7\" rx=\"5\" ry=\"7\"/>\n  </g>\n  {% if kit == \"rayados\" %}\n  <rect x=\"-19\" y=\"-9\" width=\"38\" height=\"18\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"#fff\" stroke=\"#0b2a5b\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n  <g fill=\"#0b2a5b\">\n    <rect x=\"-11\" y=\"-8\" width=\"5\" height=\"16\"/><rect x=\"-2.5\" y=\"-9\" width=\"5\" height=\"18\"/>\n    <rect x=\"6\" y=\"-8\" width=\"5\" height=\"16\"/>\n  </g>\n  {% else %}\n  <rect x=\"-19\" y=\"-9\" width=\"38\" height=\"18\" rx=\"9\" fill=\"{{ kit }}\" stroke=\"#0b1f45\" stroke-width=\"2\"/>\n  {% endif %}\n  <circle r=\"8.5\" fill=\"#8d5b3a\"/>\n  <circle cy=\"2\" r=\"7.5\" fill=\"#1d130c\"/>\n{%- endmacro %}\n\n{# Boots that stride: within each [start, end) span of the story, every 3% the\n   foot swaps between forward and back; outside the spans it rests. #}\n{% macro strides(name, first, second, spans) -%}\n  @keyframes {{ name }} {\n    {%- for start, end in spans %}\n    {% if start > 0 %}{{ start - 1 }}% { transform: none; }{% endif %}\n    {%- for t in range(start, end, 3) %}\n    {{ t }}% { transform: translateY({{ first if loop.index0 % 2 == 0 else second }}px); }\n    {%- endfor %}\n    {{ end }}% { transform: none; per second on scene pages, idle and while scrolling, in Chromium at 390x844\nwith the CPU slowed 1x, 4x and 6x (roughly a laptop, a mid-range and a budget phone).\nUsage: python fps.py\"\"\"\nfrom urllib.parse import quote\n\nfrom playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright\n\nPAGES = [\"index.html\", \"tema/partido.html\", \"tema/noticias-del-club-de-aficionados.html\",\n         \"cómo-unirse.html\"]\nMEASURE = \"\"\"async (scroll) => {\n  let frames = 0, worst = 0, last = performance.now();\n  const start = last;\n  await new Promise(done => {\n    function tick(now) {\n      frames++; worst = Math.max(worst, now - last); last = now;\n      if (scroll) window.scrollBy(0, 6);\n      if (now - start < 3000) requestAnimationFrame(tick); else done();\n    }\n    requestAnimationFrame(tick);\n  });\n  return [Math.round(frames / 3), Math.round(worst)];\n}\"\"\"\n\nwith sync_playwright() as p:\n    browser = p.chromium.launch()\n    for rate in (1, 4, 6):\n        page = browser.new_context(viewport={\"width\": 390, \"height\": 844}, device_scale_factor=3).new_page()\n        cdp = page.context.new_cdp_session(page)\n        cdp.send(\"Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate\", {\"rate\": rate})\n        for path in PAGES:\n            page.goto(\"http://localhost:8765/\" + quote(path))\n            page.wait_for_timeout(500)\n            idle = page.evaluate(MEASURE, False)\n            page.evaluate(\"window.scrollTo(0, 0)\")\n            scrolling = page.evaluate(MEASURE, True)\n            print(f\"cpu/{rate}  {path:45} idle {idle[0]:3} fps (worst {idle[1]:4} ms)\"\n                  f\"   scrolling {scrolling[0]:3} fps (worst {scrolling[1]:4} ms)\")\n    browser.close()\n","numLines":39,"startLine":1,"totalLines":39}},"displayPath":"../../../../private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b/scratchpad/fps.py"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"b8987902-2892-4804-b949-f062b268a450","timestamp":"2026-10-15T23:19:35.728Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nCalled {"parentUuid":"b8987902-2892-4804-b949-f062b268a450","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"file","filename":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b/scratchpad/t09-review.md","content":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b/scratchpad/t09-review.md","content":"## `/code-review` findings for T09 and how each was resolved\n\nThe review compared uncommitted work against `98dad86` along two separate axes, each run by its own sub-agent.\n\n### Spec (against this ticket's acceptance criteria and spec #1)\n\nNothing is missing. Every topic page, the four seeded pages, an extra page and the posts carry the right scene, in the tests and in a seeded demo export. The scene table matches row for row. Every fact in the captions matches the ticket: 13 Dec 2009, Estadio Azul, second leg, Cruz Azul 1–2 Rayados, De Nigris 54', Suazo 90', global 4–6, the 26.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Slightly off:** \"hace el gol del campeonato\" overstates the moment. At 1–1 Rayados already led 5–4 on aggregate, so Suazo's goal sealed the title rather than won it. | **Fixed.** The caption now says \"Al 90', Humberto Suazo, con el 26, sella el campeonato: Cruz Azul 1–2 Rayados, global 4–6.\" |\n| 2 | Motion (scroll-driven, played once on load, still under reduced motion) is checked by hand only. | **Kept.** The agreed test seam is the export only. Before writing tests, the owner chose not to add a CSS-shape test. The checks are by hand in headless Chromium (see Verification). |\n| 3 | The banner, stripes, stadium, disclaimer and \"no image files\" rules are not asserted by the new tests. | No change. `tests/test_t08_look.py` and `tests/test_t03_export.py` already assert them on every exported page, and they still pass. |\n| 4 | **Not asked for:** three more caption cards (minute 90, the goal, the title) besides the one naming the moment. \"Van 1–1\" is not in the ticket. | **Kept.** Before building, the owner chose the \"story stage\" layout, with about three screens of captions (13 Dec 2009 → minute 90 → the goal, 1–2 → champions, global 4–6). The reviewer checked \"1–1 at the 90th minute\" against the ticket's Wikipedia source: Cruz Azul scored at 77'. |\n| 5 | **Not asked for:** layout changes on every public page. The body is now a full-height column, `main` has a gap on top, and the footer a wider one above it. | **Kept.** These make the scene visible above and below the content card. The column keeps a short page's footer at the bottom instead of floating over its scene. |\n| 6 | Text drawn into scenes (\"ALBIAZUL\", \"ESTADIO\", \"TU LUGAR\", \"PRÓXIMOS PARTIDOS\"), and a calendar that lights up Saturdays. | **Kept.** These are signs, not logos. The calendar has no month name and no fixtures, so it claims no real dates. |\n| 7 | \"Desliza hacia abajo\" stays under reduced motion, when scrolling no longer moves the scene. | **Kept.** The reader still scrolls to read the four captions, which tell the story in words. |\n\n### Standards (CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, ADRs, and the code-smell baseline)\n\nThere are no hard violations. Published HTML has no root-absolute paths, `url(`, `<image>`, `src=` or `<script>`. Markdown still goes through `markdown.to_html`. No dependency was added, `site/` was not touched, and drafts still never reach the export.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Vocabulary: \"club page\" in a comment and a test name. CONTEXT.md says *Avoid: the club*. | **Fixed.** It is now \"the four seeded pages\", and the test is `test_each_seeded_page_carries_its_own_scene_and_any_other_page_the_default_scene`. |\n| 2 | Vocabulary: \"story\" (`.story`, `--story`) is an *Avoid* word under **Post**, used here for something with no glossary term. | **Fixed.** The new **Scene** entry names it: \"The home page's scene is the **goal story**\". The code uses \"goal story\" for that and nothing else. |\n| 3 | The banner's comment called it \"the scene\", but under the new glossary the banner is not a Scene. | **Fixed.** It now says \"the drawing\". |\n| 4 | Duplicated Code: all 11 scenes repeated the same `<svg class=\"scene …\" data-scene viewBox preserveAspectRatio aria-hidden>` wrapper. | **Fixed.** A `{% call scene(\"…\") %}` macro in `scenes/_parts.html` holds the frame (1600 × 1000, cropped around its middle, hidden from screen readers), and every scene uses it. |\n| 5 | Duplicated Code: the skin palette was retyped in 7 files, the rayas flag hand-drawn in 5, and the crowd's bob keyframe re-declared in each scene. Referee and touchline drew the same stand backdrop. | **Fixed.** `_parts.html` now has `skin(n)`, `rayas(x, y, w, h)` and `day_stand()`. The crowd macro gives each row `class=\"crowd-row\"`, and the bob is declared once in `style.css`. The fans' stand overrides it to jump. |\n| 6 | Shotgun Surgery: the goal's timing was spread over `goal.html` (keyframes), `style.css` (caption gaps by `:nth-of-type`) and `home.html` (caption order), and `--story` was defined in one file and used in another. | **Fixed.** `goal.html` holds the beats and defines the `--story` timeline. `home.html` holds each caption's gap inline, beside its text, with a comment naming the beat it lines up with. `style.css` keeps only the caption's look. |\n| 7 | Repeated Switches: the scene was chosen in three ways, and the home page's choice lived in a template. | **Fixed.** `export.py` holds every choice: `HOME_SCENE`, `TOPIC_SCENES`, and `PAGE_SCENES` with `DEFAULT_SCENE`. The home template includes `scene` like any other page, inside its story. |\n| 8 | Primitive Obsession (low): the scene is a bare string joined into a template path. | **Kept.** A test covers every value in the maps, so a typo fails `export_site`. A type for 11 template names adds nothing a reader needs. |\n| 9 | Speculative Generality (minor): the `scene-<name>` class is used only by the goal. | **Kept.** The macro now writes it in one place. Scene CSS scopes by it (`.scene-goal`, and now `.scene-fans-stand .crowd-row`). |\n| 10 | Mysterious Name (minor): `_parts.html` and the crowd macro's `cls` parameter. | **Partly fixed.** `cls` is gone, because the crowd carries its own class. **Kept:** `scenes/_parts.html` reads as \"the scenes' shared parts\", like the other `_` partials beside it. |\n\n**Verification:** `pytest` in the project venv gives 230 passed (226 before this ticket; the 4 new tests are in `tests/test_t09_scenes.py`). `mypy app scripts/seed_demo.py`, run against the venv, reports no issues. The test seams agreed before writing tests: what the export writes. That covers the home page's goal scene and caption, a scene per topic shared by its posts, a scene per seeded page with the default for any other slug, and no `<script>` on any page.\n\nThe rest was checked by hand in headless Chromium, on a site exported from the seed plus one extra page:\n\n- **Layout at 390 × 844 and 1280 × 720:** `scrollWidth == innerWidth` on the home page, all five topics, a post and all five pages, and the text sits on light cards.\n- **Scroll-driven:** with scroll-driven animation, scrolling the home page plays the run, the shot (the keeper dives the wrong way), the net, 1–1 → 1–2, the confetti and the cup, each caption passing during its beat. The Alineación magnets slide from the tray into the 4-3-3.\n- **Reduced motion:** with the reduced-motion rule applied, the home page and Alineación show their final frames.\n- **No scroll-driven support:** with the `@supports` block removed, the goal story plays once on load: running at 1 s, 1–2 at 5 s, the cup at 10 s, where it stays.\n- **Short page:** a page too short to scroll shows the final formation, and its footer stays at the bottom.\n","numLines":45,"startLine":1,"totalLines":45}},"displayPath":"../../../../private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b/scratchpad/t09-review.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"0e4d8beb-ee85-4af7-87e7-844ede36c6fc","timestamp":"2026-10-15T23:19:35.729Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nCalled the Read tool with the following input: {\"file_path\":\"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b/scratchpad/t09-review.md\"}\n</system-reminder>"},{"content":"<system-reminder>\nResult of calling the Read tool:\n1\t## `/code-review` findings for T09 and how each was resolved\n2\t\n3\tThe review compared uncommitted work against `98dad86` along two separate axes, each run by its own sub-agent.\n4\t\n5\t### Spec (against this ticket's acceptance criteria and spec #1)\n6\t\n7\tNothing is missing. No dependency was added, `site/` was not touched, and drafts still never reach the export.\n22\t\n23\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n24\t|---|---|---|\n25\t| 1 | Vocabulary: \"club page\" in a comment and a test name. CONTEXT.md says *Avoid: the club*. | **Fixed.** It is now \"the four seeded pages\", and the test is `test_each_seeded_page_carries_its_own_scene_and_any_other_page_the_default_scene`. |\n26\t| 2 | Vocabulary: \"story\" (`.story`, `--story`) is an *Avoid* word under **Post**, used here for something with no glossary term. | **Fixed.** The new **Scene** entry names it: \"The home page's scene is the **goal story**\". The code uses \"goal story\" for that and nothing else. |\n27\t| 3 | The banner's comment called it \"the scene\", but under the new glossary the banner is not a Scene. | **Fixed.** It now says \"the drawing\". |\n28\t| 4 | Duplicated Code: all 11 scenes repeated the same `<svg class=\"scene …\" data-scene viewBox preserveAspectRatio aria-hidden>` wrapper. | **Fixed.** A `{% call scene(\"…\") %}` macro in `scenes/_parts.html` holds the frame (1600 × 1000, cropped around its middle, hidden from screen readers), and every scene uses it. |\n29\t| 5 | Duplicated Code: the skin palette was retyped in 7 files, the rayas flag hand-drawn in 5, and the crowd's bob keyframe re-declared in each scene. Referee and touchline drew the same stand backdrop. | **Fixed.** `_parts.html` now has `skin(n)`, `rayas(x, y, w, h)` and `day_stand()`. The crowd macro gives each row `class=\"crowd-row\"`, and the bob is declared once in `style.css`. The fans' stand overrides it to jump. |\n30\t| 6 | Shotgun Surgery: the goal's timing was spread over `goal.html` (keyframes), `style.css` (caption gaps by `:nth-of-type`) and `home.html` (caption order), and `--story` was defined in one file and used in another. | **Fixed.** `goal.html` holds the beats and defines the `--story` timeline. `home.html` holds each caption's gap inline, beside its text, with a comment naming the beat it lines up with. `style.css` keeps only the caption's look. |\n31\t| 7 | Repeated Switches: the scene was chosen in three ways, and the home page's choice lived in a template. | **Fixed.** `export.py` holds every choice: `HOME_SCENE`, `TOPIC_SCENES`, and `PAGE_SCENES` with `DEFAULT_SCENE`. The home template includes `scene` like any other page, inside its story. |\n32\t| 8 | Primitive Obsession (low): the scene is a bare string joined into a template path. | **Kept.** A test covers every value in the maps, so a typo fails `export_site`. A type for 11 template names adds nothing a reader needs. |\n33\t| 9 | Speculative Generality (minor): the `scene-<name>` class is used only by the goal. | **Kept.** The macro now writes it in one place. Scene CSS scopes by it (`.scene-goal`, and now `.scene-fans-stand .crowd-row`). |\n34\t| 10 | Mysterious Name (minor): `_parts.html` and the crowd macro's `cls` parameter. | **Partly fixed.** `cls` is gone, because the crowd carries its own class. **Kept:** `scenes/_parts.html` reads as \"the scenes' shared parts\", like the other `_` partials beside it. |\n35\t\n36\t**Verification:** `pytest` in the project venv gives 230 passed (226 before this ticket; the 4 new tests are in `tests/test_t09_scenes.py`). `mypy app scripts/seed_demo.py`, run against the venv, reports no issues. The test seams agreed before writing tests: what the export writes. That covers the home page's goal scene and caption, a scene per topic shared by its posts, a scene per seeded page with the default for any other slug, and no `<script>` on any page.\n37\t\n38\tThe rest was checked by hand in headless Chromium, on a site exported from the seed plus one extra page:\n39\t\n40\t- **Layout at 390 × 844 and 1280 × 720:** `scrollWidth == innerWidth` on the home page, all five topics, a post and all five pages, and the text sits on light cards.\n41\t- **Scroll-driven:** with scroll-driven animation, scrolling the home page plays the run, the shot (the keeper dives the wrong way), the net, 1–1 → 1–2, the confetti and the cup, each caption passing during its beat. The Alineación magnets slide from the tray into the 4-3-3.\n42\t- **Reduced motion:** with the reduced-motion rule applied, the home page and Alineación show their final frames.\n43\t- **No scroll-driven support:** with the `@supports` block removed, the goal story plays once on load: running at 1 s, 1–2 at 5 s, the cup at 10 s, where it stays.\n44\t- **Short page:** a page too short to scroll shows the final formation, and its footer stays at the bottom.\n45\t\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"0cb99604-9df4-4255-b74b-a6b01df92d4b","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main","slug":"jazzy-stargazing-goose"}
{"parentUuid":"0e4d8beb-ee85-4af7-87e7-844ede36c6fc","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"file","filename":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Account** (*Cuenta*):\nA leader's or member's way into the admin console: an email, a password, a role, a nickname, and whether it is active. Never deleted. *Mi cuenta* is where a person sees their own.\n_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login\n\n**Temporary password** (*Contraseña temporal*):\nA password the leader sets on an account and hands over in person, for a new member or one who forgot theirs. The member can replace it on *Mi cuenta*.\n_Avoid_: Default password, reset link\n\n**Deactivate** (*Desactivar*):\nThe leader closing an account without deleting it: its person can no longer sign in, and their posts stay under their nickname. **Reactivate** (*Reactivar*) opens it again.\n_Avoid_: Delete, ban, block, suspend\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post** (*Publicación*):\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic. In Spanish, *publicación* is always the thing, never the act: for the act say *publicar*.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry; \"la publicación de …\" to mean publishing\n\n**Slug** (*Enlace*):\nThe end of a post's or page's web address, made from its title (`crónica-del-clásico-regio`). It can be changed until the post or page is first published, then never, so links shared on X or Facebook keep working. A page's slug can never be a name the site already uses for itself (the home page, the topic pages).\n_Avoid_: URL, permalink, path\n\n**Preview** (*Vista previa*):\nA post's Markdown shown exactly as readers will see it, sanitized, without saving anything.\n_Avoid_: Draft view, render\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page** (*Página*):\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted. A page is a draft until the leader publishes it; unpublishing takes it back out of the menu at the next site update. Members never see pages in the admin console.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*):\nThe number the leader gives each page. The public menu lists *Inicio*, then the published pages from the lowest number up.\n_Avoid_: Position, weight, rank\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n**Scene** (*Escena*):\nThe drawing behind a public page, which moves a little. The home page's scene is the **goal story**: Suazo's goal in the Apertura 2009 final, told as the reader scrolls. Each topic has its own scene (a post shows its topic's), each of the four seeded pages has its own, and any other page gets the default. Drawn for this site: never a crest, logo or photo.\n_Avoid_: Background image, wallpaper, hero\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft** (*Borrador*):\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted** (*Enviada*):\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public. The dashboard counts these as *Esperando revisión* (waiting for review). With pending edits, they make up the leader's review queue.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published** (*Publicada*):\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back** (*Devolver*):\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish** (*Despublicar*):\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next site update. The slug stays locked.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit** (*Cambios propuestos*):\nA member's proposed change to a published post (title, topic, body; never the slug), waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit. The dashboard counts these as *Cambios propuestos*.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve** (*Aprobar*):\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version. Readers then see *Actualizado el …* on the post, as they do after the leader edits a published post directly.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n**Site update** (*Actualizar el sitio*):\nThe leader regenerating the public site from everything published and putting it online. Readers see nothing new until a site update; publishing alone changes nothing they can see.\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), deploy, build, export\n\n**Export**:\nThe first half of a site update: writing the public site's files from everything published, wiping what was there (`cms publish`). The dashboard shows when the last one happened (*Sitio generado por última vez*).\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), build, render\n\n**Upload** (*Subir*):\nThe second half of a site update: putting the exported files online on GitHub Pages (`cms deploy`). If it fails, the export still stands and readers keep the previous site.\n_Avoid_: Deploy (in prose), push, publish\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","numLines":144,"startLine":1,"totalLines":144}},"displayPath":"CONTEXT.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"b535ebc7-4c8a-4bbc-b0e3-294ee760a11b","timestamp":"2026-10-15T23:19:35.729Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nCalled the Read tool with the following input: {\"file_path\":\"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md\"}\n</system-reminder>"},{"content":"<system-reminder>\nResult of calling the Read tool:\n1\t# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n2\t\n3\tThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. {"parentUuid":"b535ebc7-4c8a-4bbc-b0e3-294ee760a11b","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"invoked_skills","skills":[{"name":"mattpocock-skills:code-review","path":"plugin:mattpocock-skills:code-review","content":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Uncommitted T09 work against HEAD 98dad86. Ticket #10, spec #1. Only the T09 files: app/export.py, templates/public/**, tests/test_t09_scenes.py, CONTEXT.md. OUTCOME is success/error/abort/unknown.\n\n**PLAN MODE EXCEPTION — ALWAYS RUN:** This command writes telemetry to\n`~/.gstack/analytics/`, matching preamble analytics writes.\n\nRun this bash:\n\n```bash\n_TEL_END=$(date +%s)\n_TEL_DUR=$(( _TEL_END - _TEL_START ))\nrm -f ~/.gstack/analytics/.pending-\"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null || true\n# Session timeline: record skill completion (local-only, never sent anywhere)\n~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-timeline-log '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"event\":\"completed\",\"branch\":\"'$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\"}' 2>/dev/null || true\n# Local analytics (gated on telemetry setting)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ]; then\necho '{\"skill\":\"SKILL_NAME\",\"duration_s\":\"'\"$_TEL_DUR\"'\",\"outcome\":\"OUTCOME\",\"browse\":\"USED_BROWSE\",\"session\":\"'\"$_SESSION_ID\"'\",\"ts\":\"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'\"}' >> ~/.gstack/analytics/skill-usage.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n# Remote telemetry (opt-in, requires binary)\nif [ \"$_TEL\" != \"off\" ] && [ -x ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log ]; then\n  ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-telemetry-log \\\n    --skill \"SKILL_NAME\" --duration \"$_TEL_DUR\" --outcome \"OUTCOME\" \\\n    --used-browse \"USED_BROWSE\" --session-id \"$_SESSION_ID\" 2>/dev/null &\nfi\n```\n\nReplace `SKILL_NAME`, `OUTCOME`, and `USED_BROWSE` before running.\n\n## Plan Status Footer\n\nIn plan mode before ExitPlanMode: if the plan file lacks `## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT`, run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-review-read` and append the standard runs/status/findings table. If a richer report exists, skip.\n\nPLAN MODE EXCEPTION — always allowed (it's the plan file).\n\n# browse: QA Testing & Dogfooding\n\nPersistent headless Chromium. First call auto-starts (~3s), then ~100ms per command.\nState persists between calls (cookies, tabs, login sessions).\n\n## SETUP (run this check BEFORE any browse command)\n\n```bash\n_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)\nB=\"\"\n[ -n \"$_ROOT\" ] && [ -x \"$_ROOT/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\" ] && B=\"$_ROOT/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\"\n[ -z \"$B\" ] && B=\"$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist/browse\"\nif [ -x \"$B\" ]; then\n  echo \"READY: $B\"\nelse\n  echo \"NEEDS_SETUP\"\nfi\n```\n\nIf `NEEDS_SETUP`:\n1. Tell the user: \"gstack browse needs a one-time build (~10 seconds). OK to proceed?\" Then STOP and wait.\n2. Run: `cd <SKILL_DIR> && ./setup`\n3. If `bun` is not installed:\n   ```bash\n   if ! command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n     BUN_VERSION=\"1.3.10\"\n     BUN_INSTALL_SHA=\"bab8acfb046aac8c72407bdcce903957665d655d7acaa3e11c7c4616beae68dd\"\n     tmpfile=$(mktemp)\n     curl -fsSL \"https://bun.sh/install\" -o \"$tmpfile\"\n     actual_sha=$(shasum -a 256 \"$tmpfile\" | awk '{print $1}')\n     if [ \"$actual_sha\" != \"$BUN_INSTALL_SHA\" ]; then\n       echo \"ERROR: bun install script checksum mismatch\" >&2\n\n[... skill content truncated for compaction; use Read on the skill path if you need the full text]"},{"name":"mattpocock-skills:tdd","path":"plugin:mattpocock-skills:tdd","content":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"},{"name":"mattpocock-skills:implement","path":"plugin:mattpocock-skills:implement","content":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/implement\n\nImplement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.\n\nUse /tdd where possible, at pre-agreed seams.\n\nRun typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end.\n\nOnce done, use /code-review to review the work.\n\nCommit your work to the current branch.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: #10"}]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"8432097b-aa99-45e8-9d83-34b55500a8dc","timestamp":"2026-10-15T23:19:35.732Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nThe following skills were invoked EARLIER in this session (before the conversation was compacted), not on the current turn. Only continue to apply ongoing behavioral guidelines from these skills where still relevant.\n\n### Skill: mattpocock-skills:code-review\nPath: plugin:mattpocock-skills:code-review\n\nBase directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Uncommitted T09 work against HEAD 98dad86. Ticket #10, spec #1. Only the T09 files: app/export.py, templates/public/**, tests/test_t09_scenes.py, CONTEXT.md.
